title: PagedAttention (canonical fragmentation answer)
detail: The canonical statement that block-paged KV management near-eliminates fragmentation waste. Verbatim from the abstract: "we propose PagedAttention, an attention algorithm inspired by the classical virtual memory and paging techniques in operating systems. On top of it, we build vLLM, an LLM serving system that achieves (1) near-zero waste in KV cache memory and (2) flexible sharing of KV cache within and across requests to further reduce memory usage." Retained as the canonical reference because the "is paging the right primitive" question is still live (see CLOSED-12 / ABANDONED-7).

title: SGLang RadixAttention mem pool (canonical prefix-reuse pool)
detail: Canonical reference for the SGLang memory-pool design in this subsection. Verbatim from the abstract: "The runtime accelerates execution with novel optimizations like RadixAttention for KV cache reuse and compressed finite state machines for faster structured output decoding."

title: Hybrid KV cache manager — single pool, many attention types
detail: The shipped design for one shared pool across heterogeneous layer types. Verbatim: "We use a single memory pool for all layer types. The memory pool is split into multiple blocks with the same page size." The doc defines the three coordinators and states the shipped constraint verbatim: "**HybridKVCacheCoordinator**: Handles exactly two KV cache groups (must include one full‑attention group plus one other efficient‑attention group). Other cases are not implemented. You can disable prefix caching to use the KVCacheCoordinatorNoPrefixCache." Confirmed in the 0.29.0 tree: `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:591 class HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, plus `UnitaryKVCacheCoordinator` and `KVCacheCoordinatorNoPrefixCache`.

title: Decouple kernel block size from KV page size
detail: Merged PR #24486 ("[Hybrid]: Decouple Kernel Block Size from KV Page Size", author zhiyuan1i) closed issue #24280. The issue framed the problem verbatim: "in hybrid mamba/attention models the `KVCacheManager` requires the mamba and attention page sizes to match, which might cause large attention page sizes (672 tokens for nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2). On the other hand, the FlashInfer attention backend uses TRTLLM FMHA kernels for Blackwell, which require page size up to 128". The closing confirmation comment on #24280 reads verbatim: "Thanks @zhiyuan1i for merging #24486 :) I can confirm this solves the issue for nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2". The 0.29.0 tree still carries the resulting machinery: `kernel_block_size` in `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:264` with the assertion "Kernel block size {bs} must divide KV cache block size {spec.block_size}."

title: No allocation past max_model_len in the V1 block manager
detail: Page retrieved; PR metadata payload reports `"state":"MERGED"`. Title: "[V1] Do not allocate beyond the max_model_len" (WoosukKwon). GitHub lazy-loads PR conversation bodies, so the diff text was not in the retrieved payload; the merged state and title were read from the page's embedded `pullRequest` metadata. This is the V1 block-manager allocation-bound rule.

title: LIFO block reuse order in the free pool
detail: Page retrieved; metadata reports `"state":"MERGED"`. Title: "[BugFix][Core] free_blocks: restore prepend (LIFO) reuse order when prefix caching is off" (theminghuang). This settles the block-pool reuse-order question for the non-prefix-caching path.

title: Partial (sub-block) prefix cache hits for hybrid models
detail: RFC #45702 "[RFC]: Partial Cache Hits for Hybrid Models" is `stateReason=COMPLETED` (closed as completed), i.e. implemented. It states the problem verbatim: "For hybrid full-attention + Mamba models, the full-attention block size needs to be aligned with the Mamba state block size. This makes block size super large compared to before. Since vLLM prefix-cache matching is block-size granular, this coarse block size leads to suboptimal cache hit rates." and "This RFC proposes separating prefix-cache matching granularity from block size granularity. We introduce hash_block_size to allow to hit a partial cache block." The 0.29.0 tree confirms shipment: `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:84 hash_block_size: int,` and the validation "assert scheduler_block_size % hash_block_size == 0".

title: GPU-side KV events for the hybrid memory allocator (HMA)
detail: Page retrieved; metadata reports `"state":"MERGED"` and the page renders "Merged". Title: "[HMA] [KVEvent] Enable GPU-side KV events for HMA" (hickeyma). This is the allocator-side event plumbing for hybrid KV; its later attempted revert is ABANDONED-8.

title: `--mamba-block-size` and `mamba_cache_mode align` shipped flag
detail: Verified directly in the vLLM 0.29.0 source tree rather than from a PR page. `vllm/config/cache.py:177` defines `mamba_block_size: int | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)` with the docstring verbatim: "Size of a contiguous cache block in number of tokens for mamba cache. Can be set only when prefix caching is enabled. Value must be a multiple of 8 to align with causal_conv1d kernel." The CLI flag is registered at `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1293` (`"--mamba-block-size"`), gated by `vllm/config/vllm.py:2963 validate_mamba_block_size`, which raises "--mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching". A neighbouring field documents the alignment purpose verbatim: "Optional override for mamba page size; used by hybrid mamba/attention models to ensure exact alignment with attention page size."

title: Page-size unification / padding for heterogeneous layer types (the shipped allocator path)
detail: The retrieved raw source of the shipped allocator contains the unification path. `def unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size(` is at line 1365 of the retrieved copy, and its docstring says verbatim: "If not same, unify the page size by increasing the block size of layers with smaller page size. Two cases cannot be unified by block size alone and pad their physical page to the maximum instead: Mamba layers, whose page size comes from state shapes and is independent of block size; and non-MLA attention layers whose page does not evenly divide the maximum (the padded page is read through a strided view)." The retrieved file contains 11 occurrences of `page_size_padded`, including the Mamba branch that pads to the maximum page. Scope limit, stated plainly: this row covers the **padding/alignment** path only. Exact per-layer (heterogeneous) page sizes are still proposed by the open PR #56156 ("It lets hybrid attention/state-cache models retain exact per-layer page sizes using vLLM's existing packed UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs allocator instead of padding every layer to one physical page size"), and its prerequisite #56155 is also still OPEN. Do not read this row as "heterogeneous page sizes are solved".

title: Marconi-style shared-prefix admission for Mamba align mode
detail: Page retrieved; the page's embedded PR metadata reports `"state":"MERGED"`. Full title as retrieved, verbatim: "[Hybrid] Marconi-style admission policy for hybrid cache" (author s3woz). Its effect is corroborated by a later retraction comment on vLLM #54199, verbatim: "the remaining value of option (a) is smaller than the issue suggested (~+12% hit rate / ~3% TTFT on this small-model rig...)" and, on the mitigations, verbatim: "current main (16282a9c4, with #37898): 40/64 (hits at block idx 1 = floor(1500/528)*528)". The 0.29.0 tree carries it: `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:522` comment verbatim "Marconi shared-prefix junction: cache its state so sibling", and `vllm/v1/request.py:202` "hybrid/Mamba models when a shared prefix is detected (Marconi-style)."

title: vAttention — contiguous virtual memory instead of paging
detail: The canonical published counter-position to PagedAttention, still the reference for the "do we need paging" question. Verbatim from the abstract: "in trying to allocate physical memory at runtime, PagedAttention ends up changing the virtual memory layout of the KV cache from contiguous to non-contiguous. Such a design leads to non-trivial programming and performance overheads." and "vAttention is a simpler, portable, and performant alternative to PagedAttention: it supports various attention kernels out-of-the-box and improves LLM serving throughput by up to 1.23x compared to the use of PagedAttention-based kernels of FlashAttention and FlashInfer."

title: Minima-KV — mixed-format paged attention on the exact target GPU
detail: Published mixed-format paging result evaluated on the target researcher's exact accelerator class. Verbatim from the abstract: "Across separate, configuration-bound Qwen3.6-27B profiles on a single 96-GB NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, deployment accounting reports 18.3 KiB of attention KV per live token, corresponding to 3.50x compression relative to BF16 and 1.75x relative to FP8." Mechanism verbatim: "Recent and protected Anchor pages remain in FP8, while older non-anchor pages move to packed TQ3; every live-request page remains addressable. Format-specific kernels compute partial attention states and combine them through a globally normalized online-softmax merge, enabling direct heterogeneous decode without a cache-sized dense shadow."

title: PersistentKV — decode directly over native page tables
detail: Published page-aware scheduling study that executes over native block tables instead of repacking. Verbatim from the abstract: "PersistentKV maps work by KV-head group, executes directly over native page tables, and adds a compact workqueue schedule executing only non-empty row-KV-head-sequence-split tasks." Its own hedges are recorded in ABANDONED-7-adjacent notes; the headline result verbatim: "five held-out seeds improve mean wall decode-token throughput by 1.04x to 1.08x on B8 bimodal, uniform, and Zipf-like workloads, and by 1.40x on a B1 bucketed trace."

title: llama.cpp KV defrag mechanism refactor
detail: Page retrieved; the page renders "Merged" and metadata reports `"state":"MERGED"`. Title: "kv-cache : refactor the update/defrag mechanism" (ggerganov). This is the shipped answer to defragmentation in llama.cpp's unified KV cache; it is the artifact behind why llama.cpp does not expose a user-facing defragmentation threshold as a tuning knob. PR conversation body was not retrievable (lazy-loaded), so the row rests on title + merged state.

title: HMA is preserved by default for connectors that support it
detail: PR #41847 (author chfeng-cs, title "[KV Transfer] Enable HMA by default for connectors that support it") is confirmed merged on the GitHub page and is visible in the local tree as `KVConnectorFactory.supports_hma_config`. The design was worked out in issue #41830, where the author wrote: "My plan is to add a config-level helper that resolves effective HMA support from KVTransferConfig, recursing into MultiConnector children, then use that in the auto-disable path." The shipped code was re-verified on live `main` at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/vllm/config/vllm.py (lines 2018-2024): `# Auto-disable HMA only when the connector config does not support it.` and `if not KVConnectorFactory.supports_hma_config(self.kv_transfer_config):`. Its warning text states the consequence: "hybrid SSM models (e.g. Jamba, Bamba) require HMA and will fail at startup without it; models with sliding window attention will run with reduced performance."

title: `kv_load_failure_policy` ships defaulting to `fail`, and is documented
detail: The NixlConnector Usage Guide carries a "KV Load Failure Policy" section stating: "`fail` (default): Immediately fail the request with an error when KV load fails. This prevents performance degradation by avoiding recomputation of prefill work on the decode instance." and "`recompute`: Recompute failed blocks locally on the decode instance. This may cause performance `jitter` on decode instances..." The shipped default was re-verified on live `main` at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/vllm/config/kv_transfer.py (line 103): `kv_load_failure_policy: Literal["recompute", "fail"] = "fail"` with the docstring "'fail': immediately fail the request with an error finish reason (default)". It is also present in the local tree `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main`. The dedicated RFC that asked for this change, issue #32200, was nonetheless closed `NOT_PLANNED` by the stale bot — see ABANDONED-3.

title: KV role flags and the prefiller KV-block lease/heartbeat lifecycle are shipped
detail: Documented flags: "`kv_producer`: For prefiller instances that generate KV caches" and "`kv_consumer`: For decoder instances that consume KV caches from prefiller", with "`kv_role="kv_both"` is deprecated for NixlConnector." The lease mechanism is documented as: "`kv_lease_duration` (via `kv_connector_extra_config`): Lease duration (in seconds) for the prefiller's KV cache blocks. (Optional) Default: 30 ... While the request is queued on the decoder, periodic heartbeats automatically extend the lease. If neither a heartbeat nor a read notification arrives before the lease expires, the blocks are freed." Also shipped: `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl`, "Default: 480", for bidirectional multi-turn transfer.

title: Cross-topology P/D compatibility (hetero TP, block size, layout, dtype) is shipped and gated by a handshake hash
detail: The compatibility matrix separates what must match from what may differ. "What must match between P and D — By default, a `compatibility hash` is checked during handshake. P and D instances must agree on: vLLM version and NIXL connector version, Model ..., Attention backend, KV cache dtype (`cache_dtype`), EAGLE/MTP-style speculative method ..., NIXL transfer mode (push vs pull) — a push (WRITE) connector and a pull (READ) connector use incompatible transfer protocols and must never be paired." "What can safely differ between P and D: `tensor-parallel-size` (heterogeneous TP ...), `block-size` (heterogeneous block size ...), Number of KV cache blocks ...". Layout defaults are stated: "NixlConnector defaults to `LBHNC` (head-major, formerly `HND`) layout for optimal transfer performance (non-MLA models)." Dynamic quantization is refused: "`Dynamic quantization` (scales computed at runtime): ❌ Not supported. Per-block scales are not transferred alongside KV cache data."

title: Mamba1 hybrid models were added to NIXL P/D disaggregation
detail: Merged 2026-06-25 (created 2026-06-09). PR body: "Purpose Add Mamba1 hybrid-model support (e.g. Jamba) to the NIXL connector's conv-state transfer for prefill/decode disaggregation, extending the existing Mamba2/GDN path". Accuracy parity was reported across a TP sweep: "Results Accuracy parity (GSM8K, 5-shot, exact_match strict-match) across the full P_TP × D_TP sweep on an 8×H100 box". Reviewer ZhanqiuHu wrote: "Thanks for the PR! LGTM I think all the changes are safe and clean, but would you mind checking 1p4d and/or 4p1d of Nemotron or Qwen3.5 just to make sure Mamba2/GDN still works?" Note the hardware: an 8×H100 box.

title: Prefill-vs-decode engine-count tuning has shipped, documented guidance
detail: Dynamo's tuning guide has a section "Number of Prefill and Decode Engines" listing three load regimes and states: "At low load, disaggregation would not benefit much as prefill and decode are usually computed separately. It is usually better to use a single monolithic engine." It gives the ratio knob's direction explicitly: "Decrease the total amount of KV cache: Some GPUs are configured as prefill engines whose KV cache is not used in the decode phase. Since Dynamo currently allocates the KV blocks immediately when the decode engine get the requests, it is advisable to use as few prefill engines as possible (even no prefill engine) to maximize the available KV cache in decode engines." It also couples block size to transfer cost: "For block size, if the block size is too small, it leads to small memory chunks in the P->D KV cache transfer and poor performance... For most dense models, we find block size 128 is a good choice." And a live capability gap: "However, chunked prefill is currently not supported in Dynamo (vLLM backend)."

title: The shipped P/D connectors, per engine
detail: vLLM documents "Now supports 9 types of connectors", listing `ExampleConnector`, `LMCacheConnectorV1` (with `LMCacheMPConnector` multi-process mode), `NixlConnector` ("which support fully async send/recv"), `MooncakeConnector`, `MoRIIOConnector` (ROCm only), `MultiConnector`, `OffloadingConnector`, `FlexKVConnectorV1`. SGLang documents the equivalent: "Currently, we support Mooncake and NIXL as the transfer engine." (https://docs.sglang.ai/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.html). vLLM also ships a MultiConnector composition example and a `NixlConnector` multi-backend form: `"kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX", "GDS"]}`.

title: Disaggregation is officially documented as a latency/tail-ITL tool, not a throughput tool
detail: The vLLM disaggregated-prefilling page lists the two reasons — "Tuning time-to-first-token (TTFT) and inter-token-latency (ITL) separately" and "Controlling tail ITL" — and then states in a callout: "Disaggregated prefill DOES NOT improve throughput." Dynamo independently reaches the same operating-regime conclusion: "At low load, disaggregation would not benefit much as prefill and decode are usually computed separately. It is usually better to use a single monolithic engine." Both pages are shipped documentation.

title: Overlapping per-layer KV transfer with later-layer prefill was quantified and published (HMA-Serve), whose own limitations undercut the pairing
detail: HMA-Serve publishes a "compute-transfer pipeline that overlaps each layer's KV cache transfer with later-layer prefill to reduce time-to-first-token (TTFT)" and "deferred dequantization, shipping raw quantized bytes and reconstructing them lazily on the decode GPU to reduce network bandwidth and HBM usage." Treated as CLOSED because the overlap technique is published with measured results; its hardware is entirely out of reach for this researcher (see HW-2), and its cross-vendor premise is itself a limitation of the technique.

title: Reducing transferred bytes instead of overlapping transfer was published as a win under bandwidth constraints
detail: SCD states the bottleneck premise plainly: "Disaggregated serving alleviates memory bottlenecks in Large Language Model (LLM) inference but creates a severe communication bottleneck: transmitting high-dimensional Key-Value (KV) caches often dominates time-to-first-token (TTFT)." Its result: "SCD delivers up to 2.65 × TTFT speedup over the oracle consumer prefill and dominates quantization and selective recomputation baselines on the quality--latency Pareto frontier in bandwidth-constrained regimes, while keeping generation quality within 5% F1 of the oracle." Its own limitation is stated in the abstract: reuse "across heterogeneous models (e.g. base and fine-tuned variants) causes semantic misalignment that accumulates over layers, degrading generation quality."

title: FP8 KV-cache validated and repaired in vLLM
detail: A shipped, published engineering answer covering the whole FP8 KV-cache path on Hopper and Blackwell, including two kernel-level fixes and a new user-facing flag. Verbatim: "we added a two-level accumulation strategy (see SageAttention2) that writes the partially accumulated results into an actual FP32 register (flash-attention#104), which brought the FP8 accuracy back to 89%." The recommended hybrid-model invocation is shipped as a documented quick start: "vllm serve gpt-oss-20b --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers sliding_window". Also states the validated path is single-GPU: "All Hopper experiments run on a single H100 GPU using FlashAttention-3".

title: vLLM v1 KV offloading connector shipped
url: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md (retrieved from the extracted tree at `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`; the same page is served under https://docs.vllm.ai)
detail: The v1 offloading answer exists and is documented, with two specs and a stated transfer model. Verbatim: "Two specs are available, selected by the `spec_name` key in `kv_connector_extra_config`: - `CPUOffloadingSpec` (default): single CPU tier. Completed GPU blocks are copied into pinned host memory. - `TieringOffloadingSpec`: multi-tier. A CPU primary tier plus one or more secondary tiers." And: "Transfers between GPU and CPU use DMA (`cudaMemcpyAsync`) and run asynchronously alongside model computation, so offloading adds minimal CPU- and GPU-core overhead." Backing implementation is present in-tree: `vllm/v1/kv_offload/{cpu,tiering/{fs,p2p,obj}}/` including LRU and ARC policies (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/lru.py`, `arc.py`). Caveat shipped in the same doc: "This only takes effect within the process that ran the `register_cache_policy` call — it does not help when the server is launched as a separate process".

title: SGLang unified-KV pool sizing + SWA ring accounting relanded
detail: A working answer was reached after a revert-and-reland cycle. The PR page reports `state=MERGED`, `mergedTime=2026-09-07T20:13:05Z`. Commit message of `[PATCH 01/15]` verbatim: "Reland \"[AMD][DSV4] Fix unified-KV pool sizing and SWA ring accounting\" (#30315)" and "This reverts commit f5819b09bf6eb58c3f91381274e8fec994e4746a (#38163), restoring #30315 verbatim. The follow-up commit gates every remaining shared-path change behind the unified-KV switch."

title: q8_0 quantized KV cache confirmed working on llama.cpp master (claim withdrawn)
detail: The question "is quantized KV cache broken on DeepSeek-V4-Flash?" was answered in the negative, by the reporter. Verbatim: "I have to correct this report. On a clean build of current master, quantized KV cache works fine here. The issue as filed is wrong and I am closing it." The reporter's own table shows the old tree producing "gibberish, 500 peg-parse" while a clean master build gives "coherent, 14.3 t/s", concluding: "So #25202 does fix it, and the arch-scoped disable from #25391 is not needed."

title: llama.cpp Vulkan q8_0 KV dequant-once merged, but only behind a benefit gate
detail: **Corrected during verification** — this PR is merged (`merged_at: 2026-08-19T15:44:16Z`, retrieved via the search API), not closed-unmerged. The negative result lives inside it: the unconditional version of the optimization was measured as a pessimization, so a gate was added. Verbatim (comment fragment): "Testing on a 3070 - CM2 was engaging the scratch path for no benefit (slight regression, 3–6% at 16k–32k), I implemented a gate for when CM2 is engaged." The comment author was not retrievable (PR pages do not render comment bodies), so this quote is a search-API text-match fragment rather than a full-page read.

title: MTP + `--kv-cache-dtype auto` cross-sequence corruption not reproduced
detail: The reported KV-dtype/spec-decode interaction was answered by non-reproduction plus reporter attrition. Verbatim from the reporter `fank` (2026-08-06): "Not running Gemma anymore and therefor will not be able to reproduce it anymore." Independent test by `malaiwah` on a GLM-5.2 MLA stack verbatim: "**No cross-sequence bleed detected.**" The original report's scope is narrower than its title: "(Gemma-4 W4A16; fp8 KV unaffected)".

title: Structural protection, not scoring, is what makes capped KV eviction work
detail: Published working answer with a decisive positive claim. Verbatim from the abstract: "Reserving 10\% of cache at each boundary recovers 69--90\% of the $C{=}2{,}048$ reference-ceiling quality on seven LongBench models at $C{=}256$ (13\% retention); a ten-model panel spans 68--98\%." Notably in-scope for the target hardware: the regime-transfer pilot is "on Qwen3-4B (decode vs.\ prefill, $C{\in}\{512,2048\}$)" — the exact target model.

title: KV-Direct — drop the cache, checkpoint the residual stream
detail: A published, code-backed answer to "can we avoid the KV cache". Verbatim: "We prove that this state is entirely redundant: keys and values at every layer are deterministic projections of the residual stream, and recomputing them from a single residual vector per token incurs exactly zero reconstruction error, not approximately, but bit-identically." Scale is in-range: "We verify this across six models from four architecture families (135M to 4B parameters)."

title: Canonical re-examination of KV compression for production serving
detail: Published reference work with an open-sourced measurement toolkit. Verbatim (retrieved abstract; note "KV cache" appears in the raw HTML as `\texttt{KV} \texttt{cache}`, markup normalised in the quotation below): "(1) while compressing KV cache can reduce memory consumption, current implementations (e.g., FlashAttention, PagedAttention) do not optimize for production-level LLM serving, resulting in suboptimal throughput performance; (2) compressing KV cache may lead to longer outputs, resulting in increased end-to-end latency." Framing sentence: "Despite the development of many compression algorithms, their applications in production environments are still not prevalent."

title: LMCache TurboQuant KV compression shipped with documented cost
detail: A merged artifact that answers "what does KV compression cost?" with numbers. Verbatim from the PR body: `turboquant_4bit_nc` reconstruction `corr 0.995225`, `max_abs_err 0.505249` versus fp8 `corr 0.999645`; encode/decode `0.554/0.642 ms` versus fp8 `0.024/0.040 ms` (≈20× latency). Evidence level note: retrieved by the delegated LMCache/Dynamo investigation, which reported an automated substring re-verification of its quotes against saved HTML (33/33).

title: SGLang chose a hard-error guard over fixing HiCache sidecar migration
detail: The question "are HiCache host-tier hits safe with MoE routed_experts?" was answered "no, and we will fail fast rather than fix". Verbatim from `Cerdore`: "HiCache load_back relocates tokens to new slots without migrating that sidecar data, so a host-tier hit returns stale rows from whatever previously occupied the new slot. MoE is skipped on cache hits, so there's no recomputation to fix it." And: "Opened #27067 as a guard: hard error on the unsafe combo until the migration path lands. Auto-disabling either flag silently produces a different wrong result, so failing fast is the safer option." The issue itself was then closed `NOT_PLANNED` on 2026-07-10.

title: LMCache merged a revert of its own MP adapter shim
detail: Verbatim: "This reverts only the adapter shim (restores the pre-#3100 signature requiring parallel_strategy)." Merged 2026-04-23.

title: TensorRT-LLM prefix caching on VSWA models — was silently disabled, then fixed
detail: A negative result that was answered. User report, verbatim: "kv_cache_enable_block_reuse=True produces no prefix caching speedup. Repeating the exact same 4K-token prompt shows identical prefill time on cold and cached runs." Maintainer explanation, verbatim: "we gradually support SWA with reuse. The reuse was disabled due to previous cache block search tree implementation limitations." Also, verbatim: "Meanwhile please note that we are pivoting to PyTorch workflow and TRT path support might be limited." Outcome: fixed by merged PR #13346 — "The PR has been merged. Please try again @albertnanda with the latest `main`…". This is therefore a documented "prefix caching did not pay off" episode that was subsequently remediated, not an open abandonment.

title: vLLM Decode Context Parallel (DCP) for MLA — `--decode-context-parallel-size`
detail: Merged 2025-09-06. The PR body states the design contract verbatim: "You can enable DCP with --decode-context-parallel-size/-dcp xxx (only support flashmla backend now), and tp_size needs to be divisible by dcp_size, because the world size does not change by dcp, it simply reuse the GPUs of TP group, and split one TP group into tp_size//dcp_size DCP groups. e.g. with -tp 8 -dcp 8, we use 8 GPUs with -tp 8 -dcp 4, we use 8 GPUs with -tp 4 -dcp 4 -pp 2, we use 8 GPUs and kvcache token budget always increased by `dcp` times." Reviewer LucasWilkinson is quoted in the thread asking for the split naming that produced the shipped flags: "if possible, let's denote the current pr as decode-context-parallel-size and dcp_size to leave room for prefill cp in the future." The PR's own trailing section lists unimplemented sub-features: "Future work (These items will be tackled in follow-up PRs; community contributions are warmly welcomed.): DCP support MLA fullgraph … DCP support triton_mla/cutlass_mla, DCP only support flashmla backend now KV-cache deduplication via DCP in GQA (e.g., GQA8-TP16 with DCP2) … Ring-CP style prefill context parallel (PCP) implement to optimize TTFT".

title: vLLM DCP for GQA with FlashAttention (shipped)
detail: Merged 2025-10-14. Verbatim test plan in the PR body: "Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 / vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 2". Verbatim mechanism: "For the query, no collective communication is required among the DCP group. For context, the KV is distributed across different DCP ranks. This PR follows the DCP decode approach from MLA, i.e., all-gathering Q and lse, then correcting the attn out before performing reduce-scatter." The reported KV-capacity effect is in the PR body's own log lines: "[kv_cache_utils.py:859] Multiplying the GPU KV cache size by the dcp_world_size 2."

title: vLLM DCP for GQA with FlashInfer (shipped)
detail: Merged 2025-11-14. Verbatim test plan in the PR body: "export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND='FLASHINFER' vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 2". Verbatim mechanism: "FlashInfer inserts the current query KV into the cache before computation. Each query then attends to both its own KV and the context KV on the local device, with LSE applied to correct the attention outputs. In the prefill/partial-prefill stage, custom mask is added to support interleaved KV cache with FlashInfer." All three DCP backends therefore ship with TP=8 test configurations.

title: vLLM Prefill Context Parallel (PCP) basic support (shipped)
detail: Merged 2025-11-19. Verbatim PR body: "This PR, splited from full PR #26864, adds the basic supports for the Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) feature, which corresponds to DCP. … Modified files such as block_tables.py to extend the KV cache storage based on DCP & PCP; Added a communication group pcp_group for PCP; Added necessary command-line arguments to control parallelism for PCP. Temporarily disabled PCP parameters until backend support is complete, then re-enable". Note the shipped state is deliberately partial: the flags exist but backend support was gated at merge time.

title: vLLM Context Parallel Deployment doc — the written multi-GPU contract
detail: Merged 2025-10-15 by youkaichao ("add doc to explain the new DCP feature"). The doc is the canonical statement of why this technique class is multi-GPU by construction: "Say we have `N` GPUs, we can split the request into `N` chunks, and each GPU computes one chunk of the query/key/value tensors." It then makes DCP's dependency on TP explicit: "If one GPU cannot hold them all, or we want to hold more requests in the KV cache, we can first shard the KV cache along the `H` dimension, that's the plain tensor parallel sharding. It's as simple as adding `-tp <num_gpus>` to the command line." … "Then we need to add decode context parallel to further shard the KV cache along the `T` dimension. This is as simple as adding `-dcp <size>` to the command line. Note that `size` does not increase the number of GPUs we need to launch, but just reduces the KV cache duplication. The dcp size should lie in the range of `[1, tp_size/H]`." The doc also admits prefill CP was not finished at that point: "Both approaches are under active development." Its worked examples are all 8–16 GPU deployments: "For DeepSeek-R1, we have 1 kv-head when MLA is enabled. The typical single-node deployment with `-tp 8` causes 8x KV cache duplication. We can consider adding `-dcp 8` to reduce the KV cache duplication." … "When we deploy it with `-tp 16`, the KV cache duplication is 16x. We can add `-dcp 16` to completely remove the KV cache duplication". It credits the interleaving sharding idea to Moonshot and arXiv 2507.07120.

title: vLLM — Support DCP with FlashInfer MLA
detail: Merged 2026-06-29 (merged-by WoosukKwon; the page's embedded metadata records `"mergedTime":"2026-06-29T20:24:29Z"`). Verbatim PR body: "FlashInfer MLA supports LSE since flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3116 This PR can be merged once it's included in GA." title: SGLang — shipped prefill context parallelism (`--enable-prefill-cp`, `--attn-cp-size`)
detail: Shipped. The SGLang GLM-5.3 cookbook states: "Prefill context parallelism can help with reduction of TTFT under long context. To enable prefill context parallelism for GLM 5.3, please append the following arguments:" followed by the flags `--attn-cp-size 8`, `--enable-prefill-cp`, `--cp-strategy interleave`, and explains: "which splits the sequence equally across `--attn-cp-size` ranks during attention forward. The trade off for prefill CP is that it will introduce extra all-gather operation before indexer-topk and attention kernels, so it will increase latency for decode (in unified deployment) or short prefill." The referenced DeepSeek-V3.2 cookbook shows the same feature with `--cp-strategy interleave` and `--attn-cp-size 8` at "CP8", and a combined deployment path: "**PP + CP (multi-node):** Combines Pipeline Parallelism and Context Parallelism for cross-node scaling. The production-optimized configurations below have been verified on Hopper:" with the shipped multi-node invocation containing `--dist-init-addr ${prefill_master_ip}:5000`, `--nnodes 2`, `--node-rank 0`, `--tp-size 16`. The LayerSplit composition is described as: "With LayerSplit, the kv cache on each rank can be sharded over the CP attention group, and prefetched when necessary. This can reduce kv cache memory by up to 75%, thus increasing the throughput on prefill side."

title: SGLang — shipped decode context parallelism (`--dcp-size`) with an explicit MNNVL hardware gate
detail: Shipped and documented. The page's own definition: "Decode context parallelism (DCP) stripes a request's MLA KV cache across ranks in an existing tensor-parallel group. With DCP size c, rank r owns position p when p mod c = r, so each rank stores and reads roughly 1/c of the cache." Its containment rule is a hard topology constraint: "A DCP group must fit inside one attention-TP group and one attention-DP replica: Topology / attn_tp_size = tp_size / attn_dp_size / attn_tp_size % dcp_size == 0. For example, TP=64, DP=4, DCP=16 creates four valid 16-rank attention replicas. DCP=32 would cross replica boundaries and is invalid." It also documents an unfixed validation gap: "Startup currently checks only tp_size % dcp_size == 0, not the stronger condition above. Until that check is fixed, DPA+DCP deployments must enforce containment when choosing the topology." The canonical multi-GPU example: "MLA decode on DeepSeek-V3.1 with DCP 8 inside TP 8: sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1 --trust-remote-code --tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8". And a 32-GPU example: "Kimi K3 on 32 GPUs with DPA and DCP 8. The model override enables replicated Q by default; the communication backend resolves generically to fi_a2a on MNNVL systems, otherwise a2a".

title: Helix Parallelism — KV parallelism during attention, published by NVIDIA
detail: Published 2025-07-07, NVIDIA. Abstract: "We introduce Helix Parallelism, a hybrid execution strategy that applies KV parallelism during attention to shard KV caches across GPUs, then reuses the same GPUs for TP in dense LLMs or TP × Expert Parallel (EP) in MoEs during FFN computation." … "Compared to conventional parallelism approaches, Helix reduces TTL by up to 1.5x at fixed batch sizes and supports up to 32x larger batches under the same latency budget for DeepSeek-R1, pushing forward the throughput-latency Pareto on Blackwell". This is the paper vLLM's own CP deployment doc cites (arXiv 2507.07120) for DCP KV sharding, so it is the canonical reference for this cell. Critically for the hardware class, §3.1 Experimental setup says: "To evaluate the performance of different sharding strategies independent of potential feature gaps in a given software framework, we opt to leverage an in-house high-fidelity simulator modeling the latest GB200 hardware. The simulator accounts for both compute and communication costs, including latency from inter-GPU NVLink transfers, DRAM bandwidth constraints, and FLOP throughput. All performance numbers are normalized to that of the baseline to focus on the trends as opposed to specific performance claims." The evaluated models are also far outside one GPU: "(i) Llama-405B [12], a dense 405B parameter model with 128 query heads and 8 grouped KV heads (i.e., GQA attention). (ii) DeepSeek-R1 [13], a 671B parameter MoE model with MLA attention." and "we simulate decode-time inference with KV-cache sequence lengths of one million tokens and beyond."

title: Mooncake — KVCache-centric disaggregated architecture (multi-node canonical reference)
url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00079 (full HTML v3: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.00079v3); shipped connector at `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/docs/features/mooncake_connector_usage.md`
detail: Published. Abstract: "Mooncake is the serving platform for Kimi, a leading LLM service provided by Moonshot AI. It features a KVCache-centric disaggregated architecture that separates the prefill and decoding clusters. It also leverages the underutilized CPU, DRAM, and SSD resources of the GPU cluster to implement a disaggregated cache of KVCache." The vLLM connector doc states the transport requirement verbatim: "Compared to traditional caching systems, Mooncake utilizes (GPUDirect) RDMA technology to transfer data directly in a zero-copy manner, while maximizing the use of multi-NIC resources on a single machine." and lists `device_name` as "Comma-separated whitelist of RDMA devices (e.g. `"mlx5_0,mlx5_1"`) to restrict topology discovery to. Empty discovers every device. Useful on hosts exposing a mix of InfiniBand and RoCE ports, where both peers must settle on the same link layer." The shipped vLLM example is a two-host deployment: "python examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py --prefill http://192.168.0.2:8010 --decode http://192.168.0.3:8020".

title: DistServe — disaggregating prefill and decoding
detail: Published. Abstract: "DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences." §6.1 Experimental Setup is the canonical hardware statement: "Cluster testbed. We deploy DistServe on a cluster with 4 nodes and 32 GPUs. Each node has 8 NVIDIA SXM A100-80GB GPUs connected with NVLINK. The cross-node bandwidth is 25Gbps." The paper also states that even the intra-node fallback requires NVLink: "While many modern GPU clusters for LLMs are equipped with InfiniBand (e.g., 800 Gbps), in cases where cross-node bandwidth is limited, DistServe relies on the commonly available intra-node NVLINK, where the peak bandwidth between A100 GPUs is 600 GB/s, again rendering the transmission overhead negligible (see § 6.3)." The minimum viable unit in the paper's own Figure 1 framing is also >1 GPU: "Ideally, by allocating 2 GPUs for prefill and 1 GPU for decoding, we can effectively serve the model with an overall goodput of 10 rps, or equally 3.3 rps per GPU, which is 2.1x higher than existing systems."

title: Splitwise — phase splitting across separate machines
detail: Published. Abstract: "we propose Splitwise, a model deployment and scheduling technique that splits the two phases of LLM inference requests on to separate machines. … Request state is transferred efficiently between machines using optimized network libraries on the fast back-plane interconnects available in today's GPU clusters." §V-A Experimental setup is the canonical hardware statement: "To evaluate our proposal on real hardware, we implement Splitwise's KV-cache transfer mechanism on top of vLLM [51]. Our implementation is open source [1]. We run this modified vLLM on two DGX-A100 and two DGX-H10 virtual machines (VMs) on Microsoft Azure with specifications from Table I. These are the VMs used to collect the characterization data in Section III. These machines are connected with InfiniBand and the DGX-H100s have double the bandwidth (i.e., 400 Gbps)." The KV transfer design is explicitly cross-machine (Section IV-C is titled "KV-cache transfer", IV-D "Provisioning with Splitwise"); the paper's own §IV-E states: "Since Splitwise is built solely by exploiting these phases, it is applicable to all of the current and upcoming LLMs, as long as the auto-regressive nature of the workflow requires these two phases." Its characterization runs also used 8-GPU machines: "Unless stated otherwise, we run BLOOM-176B and Llama-70B on vLLM [51] on a machine with 8 H100 [16] GPUs."

title: Star Attention — sharding attention across hosts for long sequences
detail: Published 2024-11-26, NVIDIA. Abstract: "We introduce Star Attention, a two-phase block-sparse approximation that improves computational efficiency by sharding attention across multiple hosts while minimizing communication overhead." §C.2 "Hardware for Inference Speed" is the canonical statement: "In table 1, we use A100 GPUs to run the inference speedup tests. Table 7 describes the number of GPUs and the number of parallel workers used to obtain these numbers for Ring Attention vs Star Attention." Table 7 "Resources used for the speedup experiments" lists: 8B model at 16K–128K → 8 GPUs / 4 workers; 256K–512K → 16 GPUs / 8 workers; 1M → 32 GPUs / 16 workers; 70B model at 16K–32K → 8 GPUs / 4 workers; 64K → 16 GPUs / 4 workers; 128K → 32 GPUs / 8 workers. The configuration section states: "Configuration. We implement Star Attention using HuggingFace Transformers library (Wolf et al., 2020). All experiments are done on A100 GPUs with bfloat16 precision."

title: NVIDIA Dynamo — shipped multi-node inference orchestration with KV-aware routing and KVBM
detail: Shipped (README retrieved 2026-09). Verbatim: "**The open-source, datacenter-scale inference stack.** Dynamo is the orchestration layer above inference engines — it doesn't replace SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or vLLM, it turns them into a coordinated multi-node inference system. Disaggregated serving, intelligent routing, multi-tier KV caching, and automatic scaling work together to maximize throughput and minimize latency for LLM, reasoning, multimodal, and video generation workloads." The README's own "when to use this" filter is verbatim: "You're serving LLMs across **multiple GPUs or nodes** and need to coordinate them" and "If you're running a single model on a single GPU, your inference engine alone is probably sufficient." Its KV features are described as: "**KV Block Manager (KVBM)** | Offloads KV cache across GPU → CPU → SSD → remote storage | Extends effective context length beyond GPU memory" and "**ModelExpress** | Streams model weights GPU-to-GPU via NIXL/NVLink | 7x faster cold-start for new replicas" and "**Grove** | K8s operator for topology-aware gang scheduling (NVL72) | Places workloads optimally across racks, hosts, and NUMA nodes". Its headline performance number is also NVL72-only: "**7x** higher throughput per GPU | DeepSeek R1 on GB200 NVL72 w/ Dynamo vs B200 without".

title: LMCache — shipped multi-node KV cache P2P sharing, RDMA/NVLink transports
detail: Shipped. Verbatim changelog line: "[2026/01] LMCache multi-node P2P CPU memory sharing, from experimental feature to production ([blog](https://blog.lmcache.ai/en/2026/01/21/p2p-1/))." The transport requirement is stated as: "**PD disaggregation and KV transfer**: Support KV cache transfer from prefill workers to decode workers over NVLink, RDMA, or TCP through transport layers such as NIXL." Also shipped: "[2026/04] LMCache's new multiprocess (MP) architecture release". ---

title: SGLang session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache
detail: Merged by hzh0425 on 2026-08-02, titled "feat: Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache for agentic multi-turn workloads". This is the single most on-topic shipped artifact for "session-level KV management" and "KV cache growth across multi-turn agentic sessions". The stated motivation: "In multi-turn inference workloads such as agentic workflows and RL rollouts, active sessions accumulate reusable KV prefixes across turns. Under memory pressure, the standard radix cache evicts entries using only the configured cache policy, without considering whether a prefix is still referenced by an active session. This may evict an active session's prefix while unrelated, unreferenced KV remains cached, causing unnecessary recomputation in later turns and reducing cache hit rate and throughput." The mechanism: "Applications pass a stable top-level session_id with each request. When a request finishes, SGLang registers its reusable KV under that session. When the session ends, the application calls /close_session to release those references." Eviction ordering is "(is_referenced, session_ref_count, base_eviction_priority)" with "two LRU passes: unreferenced nodes first, then referenced nodes if more space is required." Importantly it is explicitly not a pin: "Referenced KV is soft-protected, not pinned. If unreferenced KV is insufficient, referenced entries remain evictable." It covers FULL attention ("tracks the reusable prefix path"), SWA ("reusable sliding-window tail") and Mamba ("reusable state at the session frontier").

title: vLLM prefix caching is ON by default
detail: Read directly from the local vLLM `main` source tree at `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main`. `CacheConfig` declares `enable_prefix_caching: bool = True` with the docstring "Whether to enable prefix caching." The hash controls are also present: `prefix_caching_hash_algo: PrefixCachingHashAlgo = "sha256"` and `prefix_cache_retention_interval` (with `0` retaining "only semantic checkpoints, including the latest replay boundary and shared-prefix junctions"). The design doc states the mechanism and its limit: "We only cache full blocks." and the workload claim "Multi-round conversation, where the user may chat with the application multiple times in the same chatting session. In this case, instead of processing the whole chatting history again and again, APC allows vLLM to reuse the processing results of the chat history across all future rounds of conversation". The doc's own Limits section: "APC does not bring performance gain when vLLM spends most of the time generating answers to the queries (e.g. when the length of the answer is long), or new queries do not share the same prefix with any of existing queries".

title: Fine-grained prefix-cache checkpoints at shared-prefix junctions (long system prompts that diverge)
detail: This shipped flag directly targets the "KV reuse across turns with changing system prompts / shared long prefix diverging mid-block" question for hybrid models. The doc states: "Under `--mamba-cache-mode align`, Mamba state is stored only on the Mamba block grid, so a prefix-cache hit can resume only at a block boundary. `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` also stores a checkpoint at the shared-prefix junction, the point where an earlier request with the same prefix stopped. Requests whose shared prefix ends inside a block can then reuse it." And the workload it is for: "This helps when many requests share a long system prompt and then diverge." Gating: "It is off by default, and takes effect only when all of the following hold: `--mamba-cache-mode align`, EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding on the Mamba group, `--prefix-match-unit` smaller than the Mamba block size, the model does not use multi-module MTP". Confirmed present in the local tree: `vllm/config/cache.py:198  enable_mamba_fine_grained_prefix_cache: bool = False` and `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1302  "--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache"`.

title: vLLM #52041 — skip MM tensor broadcast for prefix-cache-covered items
detail: Merged by njhill 2026-08-19 ("njhill merged 8 commits into vllm-project:main"). The author's framing: "The EngineCore->TP-worker broadcast was designed when request inputs were token IDs (kilobytes), so shipping them unconditionally was both correct and free. Multimodal grafted large tensors onto the same path, but for the classic workload (a fresh image per chat request) the workers genuinely need every tensor, so unconditional shipping remained necessary. What changed recently is multimodal prefix caching". This closes the question of whether prefix-cache-covered payloads can be skipped on the worker broadcast path.

title: AgentKVShift — KV reuse for agentic memory units
detail: Published 2026-05-15 (submitted), cs.AI. Directly addresses "tool-calling KV reuse / retrieval-triggered re-encoding" in agentic memory. Problem statement: "every retrieval triggers a full re-encoding of these structured memory units into Key-Value (KV) states, which dominates prefill latency. Existing training-free KV reuse methods mitigate this by selectively recomputing a small fraction of tokens, but were designed for RAG-style raw passages and degrade on structured agentic memories." Result: "AgentKVShift achieves near full recompute performance while refreshing only 10-30% of the cache... delivers prefill speedups of 2-3.5x over no-KV-reuse on a single A100." Setup verified in the full HTML: "All experiments are run on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, except for Qwen3-32B AMA-Bench evaluation and throughput profiling, which use a single NVIDIA H200 GPU due to memory and compute requirements."

title: SideQuest — model-driven KV management for long-horizon agentic reasoning
detail: Published 2026-02-26, cs.AI. Answers "how to bound KV for long chain-of-thought + retrieval-driven agentic loops". The paper states: "In such tasks, the LLM context is dominated by tokens from external retrieval, causing memory usage to grow rapidly and limiting decode performance. While several KV cache compression techniques exist for long-context inputs, we find that existing heuristics fail to support multi-step reasoning models effectively." Method: "we frame KV cache compression as an auxiliary task executed in parallel to the main reasoning task" and "Our evaluations, using a model trained with just 215 samples, show that SideQuest reduces peak token usage by up to 65% on agentic tasks with minimal degradation in accuracy". Full HTML confirms explicit compatibility with the engine's reuse machinery: "ensuring full compatibility with prefix caching to enable efficient context reuse across multiple ReAct iterations", and the serving testbed: "we compare Sidequest against the uncompressed baseline for gpt-oss-20b (Medium Effort) on the FRAMES benchmark using a single NVIDIA H100 GPU."

title: FlowKV — multi-turn isolation for KV compression
detail: Published 2025-05-21, revised v2 2025-10-08, cs.CL. The canonical answer to "repeated compression of early turns destroys multi-turn coherence". Text: "existing eviction strategies often degrade performance by repeatedly compressing early conversational context, leading to information loss and context forgetting. This paper introduces FlowKV, a novel multi-turn isolation mechanism for KV Cache management, which can be applied to any KV Cache compression method without training. FlowKV's core innovation is a multi-turn isolation mechanism that preserves the accumulated compressed KV cache from past turns. Compression is then strategically applied only to the newly generated KV pairs of the latest completed turn, effectively preventing the re-compression of older context and thereby mitigating catastrophic forgetting."

title: EpiCache — episodic KV management for long-term conversation under a fixed budget
detail: Published 2025-09-22, cs.CL. Answers multi-turn LongConvQA under a bounded KV budget without unbounded prefill peak. "EpiCache bounds cache growth through block-wise prefill and preserves topic-relevant context via episodic KV compression, which clusters conversation history into coherent episodes and performs episode-specific KV cache eviction. Across three LongConvQA benchmarks (LongMemEval, Realtalk, and LoCoMo), EpiCache improves accuracy by up to 30%, achieves near full-cache accuracy under 4-6x compression, and reduces latency and peak memory by up to 2.4x and 3.7x, respectively."

title: GrowPage — on-demand KV budgeting that preserves prefix caching
detail: Published 2026-09-03, cs.AI — inside the target window. Answers reasoning/thinking-model KV growth on a single GPU. "GrowPage maintains lightweight dual-timescale query summaries to capture recent and long-term attention behaviors, and uses their relative attention working sets to estimate demand evolution. At each capacity boundary, GrowPage either compresses KV states within the current allocation or acquires an additional physical page when broader demand emerges. By integrating with PagedAttention's page-level memory abstraction, GrowPage preserves continuous batching and prefix caching." Testbed from the full HTML: "All experiments are conducted on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80 GB memory. Following Zipage, we implement GrowPage on nano-vLLM with PagedAttention-based KV management".

title: SAECache — semantic-adaptive prefix-cache eviction with a multi-turn queue
detail: Published 2026-05-12, cs.LG. Answers "which eviction policy should a prefix cache use for agentic/multi-turn traffic". It documents the reuse-rate variance across token roles: "different token types within a prompt, including system prompts, user queries, tool outputs, model responses, and chain-of-thought reasoning, exhibit up to 756x variation in reuse rates, yet no existing eviction policy exploits this signal." Design: "a multi-queue architecture that routes KV blocks to task-specific queues with tailored priority metrics, capturing both session reuse in multi-turn requests and structural reuse in templated single-turn requests". Also records the failure mode of fixed policies: "fixed-parameter alternatives can degrade by up to 2.7x under workload mismatch". It also reports a negative integration result: "Under low-to-moderate concurrency with a single small model, vLLM's aggressive memory management rarely fills the KV cache to capacity, leading to limited eviction activity." Testbed from the HTML: a single NVIDIA A40 GPU, vLLM v0.8.5 (V0 engine), Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.

title: KVCache Cache in the Wild — production KV reuse characterization
detail: Published 2025-06-03, cs.DC. Canonical production measurement that bounds how much multi-turn reuse there really is. Abstract: "KV$ reuses are skewed across requests, where reuses between single-turn requests are equally important as multi-turn requests; the reuse time and probability are diverse considering all requests, but for a specific request category, the pattern tends to be predictable; and the overall cache size required for an ideal cache hit ratio is moderate." The HTML gives the more actionable finding for a single GPU: "The lifespan of KV$ is ephemeral: the P99 lifespan of KV$ in to-B workloads is 97 seconds, so a small cache is typically sufficient for the KV$ cache." Trace source: "we collected and characterized two representative production serving workloads from one of the world's largest cloud providers (Aliyun)".

title: Zipage — compressed paged attention that supports prefix caching
detail: Published 2026-03-01, cs.DC. Answers "can token eviction for reasoning coexist with paged/prefix-cached serving". "This paper introduces Compressed PagedAttention, a method that combines token-wise KV cache eviction with PagedAttention. We propose a comprehensive scheduling strategy and support prefix caching and asynchronous compression for Compressed PagedAttention. Based on this, we have developed a high-concurrency LLM inference engine, Zipage. On large-scale mathematical reasoning tasks, Zipage achieves around 95% of the performance of Full KV inference engines while delivering over 2.1x speedup."

title: SONIC — segment-level compression of dialogue history
detail: Published 2026-01-29, cs.CL. Answers multi-turn history compression with learned rather than heuristic eviction. "The linear growth of Key-Value (KV) cache remains a bottleneck for multi-turn LLM deployment. Existing KV cache compression methods often fail to account for the structural properties of multi-turn dialogues, relying on heuristic eviction that risks losing critical context. We propose SONIC, a learning-based framework that compresses historical segments into compact and semantically rich Nexus tokens." Reported result: "at compression ratios of 80% and 50%, SONIC consistently outperforms baselines such as H2O and StreamingLLM on four diverse multi-turn benchmarks." ---

title: vLLM prefix-cache hash algorithm selection (collision resistance)
detail: The vLLM APC design doc now documents a selectable hash algorithm and states the historical collision weakness was removed. Verbatim from the retrieved page: "In previous versions, the hash key was not guaranteed to be collision-free. As of v0.11, the default hashing algorithm is `sha256`, which addresses collision risks." On `xxhash` the page warns verbatim: "IMPORTANT: Use of a hashing algorithm that is not considered cryptographically secure theoretically increases the risk of hash collisions, which can cause undefined behavior or even leak private information in multi-tenant environments." The doc also names `sha256_cbor` as "recommended for deterministic caching across environments". Confirmed in the local vLLM source tree: `vllm/config/cache.py:145` — "default, as SHA256 is the most secure choice to avoid potential hash collisions", and `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py:34` asserts `vllm_config.cache_config.prefix_caching_hash_algo == "sha256"`.

title: vLLM reproducibility contract and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`
detail: The vLLM Reproducibility page (page footer dated April 28, 2026) gives the shipped answer for KV-dependent reproducibility. Verbatim: "vLLM does not guarantee the reproducibility of the results by default, for the sake of performance. To achieve reproducible results: In offline mode, you can either set VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 which makes scheduling deterministic, or enable batch invariance to make the outputs insensitive to scheduling. In online mode, you can only enable batch invariance." The batch-invariance page (https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/batch_invariance/, footer dated September 7, 2026, READ BODY) documents `export VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and its own limits verbatim: "Batch invariance is currently in beta. Some features are still under active development." and "Enabling batch invariance may impact performance compared to the default non-deterministic mode. This trade-off is intentional to guarantee reproducibility." Hardware requirement stated on the same page: "NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or higher." Tested models include "Qwen/Qwen3-4B-AWQ" and "Qwen/Qwen3-8B". Note the causal link to KV: the source tree shows cascade attention is switched off under this flag — `vllm/config/vllm.py:1795-1800`: "Disabling cascade attention when VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT is enabled."

title: vLLM tiered KV offloading with a filesystem (disk) secondary tier
detail: Blog dated September 10, 2026 (authors Or Ozeri, Danny Harnik, Ronen Schaffer, Itay Etelis, Varun Sundar Rabindranath). Verbatim: "The framework has been available in vLLM since v0.22 and a detailed usage guide can be found here." The filesystem tier is documented verbatim as: "Stores each KV chunk as a file on local or networked storage. Uses content-addressed naming — identical token sequences map to the same key, so matching inputs share cached data automatically." with "Highlights: Non-blocking lookups / Atomic writes / Separate read/write thread pools". Config verbatim: `"secondary_tiers": [{"type": "fs", "root_dir": "/mnt/kv-cache"}]`. The blog's own benchmark setup is H100-class multi-GPU (see HW-1 below), but the feature itself carries no such requirement. Also verbatim on the reload path: "the scheduler receives a RETRY and re-checks on the next cycle."

title: vLLM prefix-cache hit-rate counters and their design rationale
detail: The Metrics design doc lists verbatim: "`vllm:prefix_cache_queries` (Counter) - Number of prefix cache queries." and "`vllm:prefix_cache_hits` (Counter) - Number of prefix cache hits." Under "Prefix Cache metrics" the doc explains the measurement choice verbatim: "Every time the prefix cache is queried, we record the number of tokens queried and the number of queried tokens present in the cache (i.e. hits). However, the metric of interest is the hit rate - i.e. the number of hits per query. ... To achieve this, we should record the queries and hits as counters in Prometheus, rather than recording the hit rate as a gauge." It also documents the logging-side estimator verbatim: "The prefix cache hit rate over the most recent 1k kv-cache block queries". Confirmed in the local source: `vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py:584-601` defines `vllm:prefix_cache_queries` / `vllm:prefix_cache_hits`.

title: vLLM KV block residency/eviction metrics
detail: Section "KV Cache Residency Metrics" verbatim: "We also emit a set of histograms that describe how long sampled KV cache blocks stay resident and how often they are reused. Sampling (`--kv-cache-metrics-sample`) keeps the overhead tiny; when a block is chosen we record: lifetime – allocation ⟶ eviction; idle before eviction – last touch ⟶ eviction; reuse gaps – the pauses between touches when the block gets reused". The exposed Prometheus metric names verbatim: "`vllm:kv_block_lifetime_seconds` – how long each sampled block exists. `vllm:kv_block_idle_before_evict_seconds` – idle tail after the final access. `vllm:kv_block_reuse_gap_seconds` – time between consecutive touches." Stated use verbatim: "Looking at lifetime and idle time on one chart makes it easy to spot stranded cache or workloads that pin prompts for a long decode."

title: vLLM KV-connector (external/offloaded) prefix cache hit-rate stats
detail: Merged PR; page header verbatim: "NickLucche merged 6 commits into vllm-project:main". Purpose verbatim from the PR body: "Add prefix-cache metrics for KV connectors / Introduces connector-agnostic metrics to track KV connector cache efficiency, enabling clearer insights into cache effectiveness and overall system performance." The metrics appear in the local source tree as `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries` and `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits` (`vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py:608-629`). Note the review finding about the hit-rate denominator, which is itself relevant to hit-rate measurement: the gemini-code-assist bot wrote verbatim "The number of queries to the connector cache is being miscalculated. request.num_tokens represents the total prompt length, but the query to the connector is only for the tokens not found in the local prefix cache. Using the total prompt length overestimates the number of queries and will lead to an incorrectly low hit rate metric."

title: vLLM "prefix cache hit rate == 0" for gpt-oss-style hybrid models
detail: Page header verbatim: "heheda12345 merged 3 commits into vllm-project:main", dated Feb 2, 2026. Title: "[Fix] prefix cache hit rate == 0 bug with gpt-oss style models". Cross-referenced from the issue it closed: vLLM #32802 "[Bug]: GPT-OSS 0% prefix cache hits with hybrid attention + EAGLE" is CLOSED with `state_reason=COMPLETED`, and the closing comment by benchislett (2026-04-07) verbatim: "Seems like this was fixed by #33524". This CLOSED item carries a documented residual limitation (see ABANDONED-9).

title: vLLM selective prefix-cache retention for sliding-window KV cache (DSv4)
detail: Page header verbatim: "ywang96 merged 13 commits into vllm-project:main", Jun 4, 2026. PR body verbatim: "DeepSeek v4 now exhibits very low effective prefix cache capacity. For example, on TP8 with 8xB300, the reported KV cache capacity is ~14.5x concurrency. However, a microbenchmark that sends 1M-context requests sequentially shows that after the second request is sent, replaying the first request already begins to miss the prefix cache. This means the practical prefix-cache re..." (truncated by page rendering). This is the merged structural fix that superseded the failed protection-layer PRs in ABANDONED-3/4/5.

title: SGLang deterministic inference and its radix-cache compatibility matrix
detail: Documents `--enable-deterministic-inference` (flag; default: disabled). The page states the root cause verbatim: "The main source is varying batch sizes. Different batch sizes cause GPU kernels to split reduction operations differently, leading to different addition orders. Due to floating-point non-associativity ((a + b) + c ≠ a + (b + c)), this produces different results even for identical inputs." It claims verbatim: "Building on Thinking Machines Lab's batch-invariant operators, SGLang achieves fully deterministic inference while maintaining compatibility with chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, radix cache, and non-greedy sampling." The feature-compatibility table for the KV-relevant axis reads verbatim: FlashInfer → Radix Cache "❌ No"; FlashAttention 3 (FA3) → Radix Cache "✅ Yes"; Triton → Radix Cache "✅ Yes". It also ships a radix-specific determinism test verbatim: "python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode radix_cache" with "Expected result: All tests should show `Unique samples: 1` (perfectly deterministic)." This documented "FA3 + radix = Yes" is directly contradicted by ABANDONED-1.

title: SGLang HiCache L1/L2/L3 including a file (disk) backend
detail: Verbatim: "HiCache organizes GPU memory as L1, host memory as L2, and distributed storage as L3." and "The file backend writes to /tmp/hicache by default (SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR overrides it), which is node-local unless that path is a shared mount." A directly relevant scope limitation is stated verbatim: "L2 is node-local and instance-private. It is host memory owned by one inference instance's process, so two instances never read each other's L2, not even two instances on the same node. A KV cache produced by instance 0 becomes visible to instance 1 only after it reaches L3."

title: SGLang observability — metrics, request dump/replay, crash dump/replay
detail: Verbatim: "SGLang exposes the following metrics via Prometheus. You can enable them by adding `--enable-metrics` when launching the server." For reproducibility of KV-dependent results, the page ships verbatim: "You can dump all requests and replay them later for benchmarking or other purposes. ... The server will dump the requests into a pickle file for every 100 requests. To replay the request dump, use `scripts/playground/replay_request_dump.py`." plus "SGLang can preserve recent request data for replay and collect CUDA device coredumps for low-level debugging. Set the crash diagnostics folder with `--crash-dump-folder /tmp/crash_dump`."

title: SGLang HiCache consistency fix plan under pipeline parallelism
detail: Issue "[PP + HiCache] HiCache Consistency Fix Plan" by whybeyoung, created 2026-04-12, `state=CLOSED`, `stateReason=COMPLETED`. Cross-checked against an independently filed, still-OPEN inconsistency in the same subsystem (see OPEN-13, SGLang PR #30850), so the "completed" scope here is the PP-specific plan, not HiCache correctness in general.

title: Prefix caching measurably changes agent trajectories (published measurement)
detail: Title "Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving", submitted 2026-09-04. Verbatim from the abstract: "Enabling the cache changed the agent's trajectory on 36.2 percent of episodes at 16-bit precision and on 75.0 percent at four-bit, a gradient that survives re-measurement under a controlled cache configuration. With caching disabled, repeated execution was bit-identical in every configuration, 0 of 800 episodes, which bounds other sources of nondeterminism at 0.5 percent." and the mechanism claim verbatim: "Cached serving is deterministic given cache state, and irreproducible in practice because that state is absent from the request and never reset by default." Hardware (retrieved from https://arxiv.org/html/2609.04748v1, READ BODY): "All measurements ran on a rented NVIDIA RTX 4090 with 24 GB of memory" — inside the target researcher's single-GPU envelope.

title: Eviction error certificates via randomized eviction design
detail: Title "Error Certificates for KV-Cache Eviction via Randomized Design", submitted 2026-07-23, rev 2026-08-29. Verbatim: "We replace the deterministic tail with Poisson sampling at known inclusion probabilities, which makes the eviction error identifiable and turns a survey-sampling variance estimator over the retained set into a per-step error certificate at one extra scalar per retained token." and the impossibility result verbatim: "We prove that no estimator computable from the information a deterministic scheme retains is consistent for its own eviction error: evicted values can be altered so that everything retained is unchanged while the true attention-output error grows without bound." Reported coverage verbatim: "the certificate covers the realized attention error in 96.9--97.7\% of 12{,}096 replay cells and in 98.1--99.7\% on twelve further architectures."

title: Matched-budget audit showing the compression-evaluation protocol decides the ranking
detail: Title "How Query Visibility Changes KV-Cache Compression Rankings: A Matched-Budget Audit", submitted 2026-07-11. Verbatim: "KV-cache compression methods are predominantly evaluated with the query appended to the context before compression -- a query-aware protocol. Yet the economic case for a compressed KV cache is reuse: compress a document once, answer many future questions against it." and "Three findings. (1) Query visibility changes the rankings: under the agnostic protocol, of the five audited methods that share a common attention backend, only KeyDiff beats a best-of-3 trivial baseline consistently (31 of 36 cells), and the most widely deployed method, SnapKV, loses to "keep the start and the recent window" on average (-0.066)." Scale verbatim: "144,300 paired evaluations on RULER-8192; 40,800 on LongBench; 50,000-resample paired bootstrap throughout".

title: Runtime observability contract that localizes silent KV corruption
detail: Title "Runtime Observability for Heterogeneous Attention Memory", submitted 2026-08-06, rev 2026-08-16. Verbatim: "Applied to a served DeepSeek-V4 stack with a packed compressed-KV prototype, the same machinery localizes a silent corruption to a precise structural boundary -- exact in the eviction-free, identity-isolated regime, with every observed failure in an eviction or slot-reuse regime". Also verbatim on honest tiering: "every claim is certified, partially certified, or empirical, composition inherits the weakest tier, and the tier is decided by the machine." Hardware is in HW-4.

title: SSD-resident KV without the kernel filesystem
detail: Title "Unified KV Pooling to Accelerate Long-Context LLM Serving", submitted 2026-06-10. Verbatim: "unified KV pooling, which aggregates multiple host-memory modules and SSDs into a single logical pool and distributes KV caches across devices based on their bandwidth. To eliminate the filesystem overhead, we design KV-passthrough, which bypasses the kernel filesystem and directly accesses SSD-resident KV caches from user space via SPDK." Reported result verbatim: "unified KV pooling reduces TTFT in long-contexts ~4.1x over state-of-the-art techniques, all making under 10 s. It also reduces blocked I/O time by up to 23.2x by eliminating filesystem overhead." Retrieved testbed sentence verbatim (this is a single-GPU setup, so NOT hardware-ruled-out): "We use Qwen3-30B-A3B [18] on a server equipped with an NVIDIA H100-80GB GPU, two 64 GB DDR4 host-memory modules with a combined peak bandwidth of 21.3 GB/s, and two 2 TB NVMe SSDs connected through PCIe 5.0×16 with a combined peak bandwidth of 63 GB/s." Its own limitation, verbatim: "Our current implementation relies on SPDK polling for SSD I/O completion. While polling eliminates the kernel interrupt path and reduces I/O latency, it increases CPU utilization due to continuous queue checking."

title: vLLM Automatic Prefix Caching (hash-based block cache)
detail: The canonical vLLM design doc for prefix KV reuse, retrieved live. It states the value proposition and the implementation choice verbatim: "Since prefix caching is almost a free lunch and won't change model outputs, it has been widely used by many public endpoints (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and most open source LLM inference frameworks (e.g., SGLang)." And: "While there are many ways to implement prefix caching, vLLM chooses a hash-based approach." The doc specifies the key components and two hard constraints: "We only cache full blocks." And on hashing: "In previous versions, the hash key was not guaranteed to be collision-free. As of v0.11, the default hashing algorithm is `sha256`, which addresses collision risks." Corroborating local tree evidence (not a URL): `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/vllm/config/cache.py:139` reads `enable_prefix_caching: bool = True`, i.e. prefix caching is on by default in the extracted 0.29-era tree, and `prefix_caching_hash_algo: PrefixCachingHashAlgo = "sha256"` at line 141.

title: Per-request `cache_salt` for prefix-cache isolation, hardened against DoS
detail: The design doc documents salting as shipped: "By including a `cache_salt` in the request, this value is injected into the hash of the first block, ensuring that only requests with the same salt can reuse cached KV blocks. This prevents timing-based attacks where an adversary could infer cached content by observing latency differences. This offers protection without compromising performance." The mechanism is an extra hash component: "Extra hashes: Other values required to make this block unique, such as LoRA IDs, multi-modality input hashes (see the example below), and cache salts to isolate caches in multi-tenant environments." The parameter was later hardened by merged PR #54353 ("[Bugfix] Bound cache_salt length to prevent DoS via scheduler CPU exhaustion", merged 2026-08-30), whose body reads verbatim: "Adds `max_length=1024` to the `cache_salt` Pydantic `Field` on all six API protocol models: completions, chat completions, responses, pooling, Anthropic, and scale-out (token-in-token-out)." with the threat being an attacker able to send "arbitrarily large salt strings that are serialized via `pickle.dumps` + `sha256` on the single-threaded EngineCore scheduler, stalling all concurrent requests."

title: SGLang RadixAttention (canonical reference)
detail: The canonical paper behind SGLang's radix-tree prefix reuse, retrieved from arXiv (submitted 12 Dec 2023, v2 6 Jun 2024). Verbatim from the abstract: "The runtime accelerates execution with novel optimizations like RadixAttention for KV cache reuse and compressed finite state machines for faster structured output decoding." Reported result, verbatim: "Experiments show that SGLang achieves up to 6.4x higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art inference systems on various large language and multi-modal models on tasks including agent control, logical reasoning, few-shot learning benchmarks, JSON decoding, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and multi-turn chat." This remains the reference implementation that later 2026 work (vLLM hybrid checkpoints, HiRadixTree, granularity papers) cites.

title: SGLang radix cache eviction policies (lru / lfu / slru / priority)
detail: A shipped, documented eviction-policy surface for the radix cache, retrieved as clean markdown. Verbatim: "Select one with `--radix-eviction-policy`. All of them fall back to least-recently-used order within a tie." Policy semantics are documented per row, e.g. "`lfu` | The prefix with the fewest cache hits, then the least recent." and "`slru` | Prefixes still in the probationary segment, then the least recent within a segment." Two important scoping statements: "A policy only scores. It does not decide how much to free, and it cannot pin KV in memory — a node protected by the policy is still evicted if reclaiming everything else is not enough." and "`fifo`, `mru`, and `filo` also exist in the policy registry but are not offered on the command line. They are reachable only by out-of-tree code that extends the choice list, and exist for experiments rather than serving." The doc also states the tradeoff explicitly: "`lfu` and `slru` help when your traffic has a stable hot set that a recency-only policy keeps flushing; they hurt when prefix popularity shifts over time, because a prefix that earned a high hit count keeps its advantage after it stops being useful."

title: SGLang session-aware radix cache (soft-pinned KV per session)
detail: Shipped multi-turn/agent KV retention feature. Verbatim: "This feature is implemented only by `UnifiedRadixCache`." Invocation: `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 ... --enable-session-radix-cache`. Limits are documented up front: "Session references are soft protection, not memory pins. Referenced KV can still be evicted when reclaiming unreferenced KV is insufficient." Eviction order is spelled out per cache component, including hybrid ones: "Full attention | The reusable prefix path from the registered leaf to the root | Unreferenced nodes first, then referenced nodes with fewer session references, then the configured policy such as LRU" and "Mamba | The reusable state on the registered leaf | Two LRU passes: unreferenced nodes first, then referenced nodes if more space is required". Also: "UnifiedRadixCache still applies component cascade rules. Evicting an internal Full node also evicts its SWA and Mamba data; evicting SWA also evicts Mamba data; evicting Mamba affects only Mamba."

title: SGLang HiCache L3 cross-instance prefix sharing
detail: This is the shipped answer to "can prefix KV be shared across instances". Verbatim tier statement: "L2 is node-local and instance-private." and "This is the answer to a common question: HiCache cannot pool the host memory of several machines into one larger L2. Growing `--hicache-ratio` or `--hicache-size` only makes each instance's own private L2 larger. Cross-instance reuse is the job of L3, so it needs `--hicache-storage-backend`." On the mechanism: "**Cross-instance Sharing**: When data is written back from L2 to L3, only data not already present in L3 is transferred. KV caches stored in L3 can then be shared across all SGLang instances in the cluster (depending on the L3 backend implementation), significantly improving cache hit rates within the same memory budget." Backends are enumerated verbatim: "Distributed backends such as `mooncake`, `hf3fs`, `nixl` and `aibrix` give cluster-wide scope, but only when every instance is pointed at the same namespace and configuration." The metadata structure is described as "HiRadixTree", extending RadixAttention: "HiRadixTree extends this idea: each node corresponds to the KV cache of a span of consecutive tokens and records where that KV cache is stored—whether in local GPU memory, CPU memory, L3 storage, or multiple of these tiers."
