title: SGLang SMG router cache-aware routing policy
detail: The shipped cache-aware routing policy, retrieved as markdown. Verbatim: "**Cache-Aware Policy (Default, Recommended)**" and "The cache-aware policy provides the best performance for most workloads". The mechanism list is verbatim: "1. Maintains an approximate radix tree for each worker based on request history 2. Routes requests to workers with the highest prefix match (cache hit) 3. Falls back to shortest-queue routing when load is imbalanced 4. Automatically evicts old entries to prevent memory overflow". Flags: `--policy cache_aware --cache-threshold 0.5 --balance-abs-threshold 32 --balance-rel-threshold 1.5 --eviction-interval-secs 120 --max-tree-size 67108864`. The same doc contrasts the non-router baseline: "No cache-aware routing", and reports "✅ Yes - significantly higher cache hit rate" for cache awareness, with an 8×A100 dp-size=8 benchmark attributed to the SGLang v0.4 blog.

title: vLLM internal prefill checkpoints for Mamba prefix caching (hybrid align mode)
detail: Merged 2026-08-22 (state MERGED confirmed in the retrieved page payload). The problem statement is verbatim: "Mamba prefix caching currently splits a prefill at the last block boundary" with the before/after given as "Model forward (7680 tokens) -> FlashKDA(7680 tokens) -> save checkpoint -> Model forward (320 tokens) -> FlashKDA(320 tokens)" becoming "Model forward (8000 tokens) -> FlashKDA(7680) -> save checkpoint -> FlashKDA(320)". Benefit verbatim: "This PR helps us avoid a second full-model pass through attention, MoE, routing, and TP collectives." Title carries the measured result: "9%~25% TTFT improvement". Validation command uses `vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code -tp 8 ... --enable-prefix-caching`. This answers "can a recurrent-state hybrid model actually get prefix-cache hits at all", and it supersedes the pre-existing state documented as open in the hybrid KV manager doc (see CLOSED-12).

title: vLLM hybrid prefix caching with spec-decode rewind and partial (sub-block) hits
detail: Merged 2026-09-06. Verbatim purpose: "Extend the Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoint optimization from #52789 to support: speculative decoding / Eagle block rewind; partial prefix caching ( prefix_match_unit < Mamba block size ); and checkpoint blocks restored through KV connectors such as MooncakeStore." The correctness invariant is stated verbatim: "The cache manager and FlashKDA worker share the same checkpoint-validity rules, so a checkpoint block is allocated and hashed only when the worker can write it." Re-keying is described: "For an aligned partial checkpoint, the already reserved request-owned checkpoint block is re-keyed from its provisional boundary to the state position actually exported by FlashKDA. This PR keeps the block allocation, eviction, and free lifecycle introduced in #52789 ." Note that the validation hardware is TP8/EP8 across two 4-GPU nodes — the feature itself is not gated on it, but the reported numbers are.

title: vLLM fallback when a hybrid KV group cannot answer fine-grained lookups
detail: Merged 2026-08-12. This is the shipped answer to the "fine-grained hits are silently disabled" failure mode. Verbatim summary: "Fine-grained prefix-cache hits are enabled for hybrid models containing Mamba `align` groups. However other groups, such as a sliding-window DSpark drafter, may use KV cache managers that only support block-aligned lookups. This previously caused an assertion when prefix caching was enabled." The change list: "Enables fine-grained hits only when every KV cache manager supports the required lookup granularity." / "Falls back to scheduler-block-aligned prefix hits for incompatible layouts." / "Prevents the scheduler from creating partial-tail cache entries after that fallback." / "Logs when fine-grained hits are disabled." The PR also documents its own cost verbatim: "Short and medium prompts may receive no prefix-cache reuse because hits must land on the much larger scheduler alignment." Reported result: "Repeated 66,007-token prompt reused 57,600 tokens."

title: vLLM retention interval for the offloading connector (prefix caching × KV offload × sliding window)
detail: Merged 2026-09-04. Verbatim purpose: "Add retention interval support to `OffloadingConnector`. The Mooncake KV connector supports retention interval support via the `envs.VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` env variable. It is used to avoid storing/loading blocks that are outside of the sliding window of the attention mechanism. This is implemented via block masks. The implementation in `OffloadingConnector` uses the same block mask mechanism to implement retention interval support." Test evidence is on gpt-oss-20b (a sliding-window hybrid) with `--enable-prefix-caching` and the CPUOffloadingSpec.

title: Hybrid KV Cache Manager (layer-type-specific prefix-cache rules)
detail: The shipped design for making one block pool serve full-attention, sliding-window and Mamba groups with a single page size. Verbatim: "Support layer-specific prefix-cache rules, for example: Full attention: a cache hit prefix requires **all** tokens remain in the KV cache. Sliding window: a cache hit prefix only requires the last **`sliding_window_size`** tokens remain in the KV cache." The coordinator surface is named: `KVCacheCoordinatorNoPrefixCache`, `UnitaryKVCacheCoordinator`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, with "Handles exactly two KV cache groups (must include one full‑attention group plus one other efficient‑attention group). Other cases are not implemented." Two candid limitations are in the doc itself: the overall banner "This feature is still in its early stage and things may change."; the grouping heuristic "This case happens in Gemma-3 series models... The solution has some memory waste and is not perfect."; and for Mamba, at the time of writing, "The prefix caching support of the mamba model is work in progress." (that last sentence is the pre-CLOSED-8 state; see also OPEN-4). ---

title: vLLM pluggable KV cache eviction policy (CPU/offload tier)
detail: PR #37874 "[KV Offload] Refactor CPU offloading: pluggable CachePolicy, remove Backend abstraction, restructure into `cpu/` package" was merged by `orozery` (Or Ozeri) at `"mergedTime":"2026-03-24T05:02:51Z"` with `"state":"MERGED"`. The user-facing knob is documented in the shipped vLLM docs, retrieved from the local vLLM tree at `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`: "`eviction_policy` resolves through `CachePolicyFactory` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/factory.py`), which pre-registers the built-in `lru` and `arc` policies." The same doc gives the reference table row: "| `eviction_policy` | no | `lru` | both | Primary tier policy: built-in `lru`/`arc`, or a custom `CachePolicy` name (see [Custom Eviction Policies](#custom-eviction-policies)). |" and an out-of-tree extension path: "Implement `CachePolicy` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/base.py`) in your own package — no vLLM fork or patch required". Source confirms the default: `self.eviction_policy: str = self.extra_config.get("eviction_policy", "lru")` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py`). `ARCCachePolicy` implements T1/T2/B1/B2 adaptive replacement (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/arc.py`).

title: SGLang radix-cache eviction policy selection
detail: SGLang ships a selectable prefix-cache eviction policy. Verbatim from the docs page: "Select one with `--radix-eviction-policy`. All of them fall back to least-recently-used order within a tie." The documented policy set is `lru` (default), `lfu`, `slru`, and `priority`, with the table row "slru | Prefixes still in the probationary segment, then the least recent within a segment. Like `lfu`, but you want a hard floor on how much a one-off prefix can displace a proven one." Parameterisation is shipped too: "Some policies take parameters. Pass them as a json object to `--radix-eviction-policy-config`". The page also names the shipped limits: "A policy only scores. It does not decide how much to free, and it cannot pin KV in memory — a node protected by the policy is still evicted if reclaiming everything else is not enough." and "Hit count (`lfu`, `slru`) counts how many times a node was matched by a later request. It is not incremented for chunked-prefill steps, for evicted nodes, or under write-back HiCache."

title: TriAttention shipped in TensorRT-LLM
detail: PR #16957 `"[None][feat] Add TriAttention KV-cache compression method"` by `Hudayday` shows `"state":"MERGED"` and `"mergedTime":"2026-08-04T00:13:38Z"`. Verbatim from the PR description: "Add TriAttention NVIDIA work @ ICML 2026 KV-cache compression support to the TensorRT-LLM." and "TriAttention is a training-free decode-time eviction algorithm: every beta confirmed generation tokens, it scores the evictable decode region using offline per-head query calibration, keeps budget important tokens, compacts their K/V data in place, and releases unused tail pages." Reported result, verbatim: "On Qwen3-8B, TriAttention (B=2048, β=2048) delivers up to 1.61× the throughput of the Dense baseline at the same batch size". See HW-1 — the merge is real but hardware-scoped.

title: NVIDIA/kvpress — shipped eviction-method library
detail: Verbatim from the README (retrieved from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/kvpress/main/README.md`): "kvpress implements multiple KV cache compression methods and benchmarks using 🤗 transformers, aiming to simplify the development of new methods for researchers and developers in this field." The library ships implementations of essentially every method named in this subsection, e.g. "`SnapKVPress` ...: average attention weight of the last queries", "`StreamingLLMPress` ...: keep only the initial and recent tokens", "`PyramidKVPress` ...: maintain pyramid-like cache sizes, allocating more cache budget to lower layers and less to higher layers", "`AdaKVPress` ...: prune bottom scores of any `ScorerPress` but across all heads, achieving head-wise compressions", "`CriticalKVPress` and `CriticalAdaKVPress` ...: refine the scores using the L1 norm of Wo @ values, coupled with a two-stage selection.", and decoding-phase compression via `DecodingPress`. Install is a plain `pip install kvpress`.

title: Ada-KV published (NeurIPS 2025) and integrated into vLLM by Cloudflare
detail: Verbatim from the repo README: "AdaKV has been accepted at NeurIPS 2025! 🎉" and, on community adoption: "kvcompress The Cloudflare team integrates Ada-KV into vLLM—an impressive and cool example of industrial deployment." The paper itself (retrieved at https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.11550, comments field `NeurIPS 2025`) states: "we propose {\it Ada-KV}, the first head-wise adaptive budget allocation strategy. It offers plug-and-play benefits, enabling seamless integration with prior cache eviction methods." Ada-KV is also the head-wise budget reference used by later negative results below.

title: Attention sink tensors fixed in vLLM's FlashAttention cascade path
detail: PR #26325 "[Bugfix] Add missing sink tensor into flash attn cascade attn implementation" by `plliao`. Verbatim from the rendered page: "simon-mo merged 4 commits into vllm-project:main vllm-project/vllm:main from plliao:fix_flash_attn_cascade_attn_sink_tensor". This is the attention-sink feature (used by models such as gpt-oss) actually reaching the decode kernel path rather than only being plumbed in config. The local vLLM tree corroborates that sinks are a supported-and-tested backend capability: `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py:310: invalid_reasons.append("attention sinks not supported")`, and tests exist at `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py:1062: def test_flashinfer_attention_sinks_refreshed_after_reload(dtype)`.

title: Attention sinks are provably necessary (theory)
detail: Verbatim from the abstract: "We prove that, in some settings, it is the latter: computing a trigger-conditional behavior necessarily induces a sink in softmax self-attention models." and "We also prove that non-normalized ReLU attention can solve the same task without any sink, confirming that the normalization constraint is the fundamental driver of sink behavior." This closes the question of whether the sink is merely an optimization artifact — a result relevant to any eviction policy that treats position-0 as a disposable token.

title: Recency/Frequency (ARC-style) adaptive KV block caching for vLLM
detail: Verbatim from the abstract: "Existing cache management strategies adopt the least-recently-used policy for evicting cache blocks. However, LRU leads to multiple unrelated workloads flushing each other's caches. To address this, we integrate adaptive caching that dynamically allocates cache space between recently and frequently occurring KV blocks." Reported effect, verbatim: "it improves the KV cache hit rate by up to 10.8% and reduces time to first token by up to 12.6% over naive vLLM on synthetic document question answering workloads, and 2.1% and 2.0% respectively on real-world conversation workloads." Publication venue, verbatim: "Accepted at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Resource-Adaptive Foundation Model Inference (AdaptFM)". Note the small real-workload gains (2.1% / 2.0%) versus the 10.8% / 12.6% synthetic figures.

title: CacheWise — reuse-aware eviction for coding-agent workloads, implemented in vLLM
detail: Verbatim from the abstract: "CacheWise combines prefix-aware scheduling with reuse-aware eviction guided by lightweight predictions from tool call metadata. Implemented in vLLM and evaluated on the collected traces, CacheWise reduces KVCache evictions by up to 2-2.6x and improves total agent session completion time by up to 3.5x." The paper's own framing of the deficiency it targets, verbatim: "coding agent sessions repeatedly reuse large prefixes and create sustained KVCache pressure that conventional LLM serving policies handle poorly." ---

title: FP8 e4m3 per-tensor KV cache, calibration-free (scale = 1.0), validated Hopper + Blackwell
detail: vLLM's flagship FP8 KV-cache validation. The flag quantises both storage *and* the attention matmuls. Verbatim: "vLLM's --kv-cache-dtype fp8 flag quantizes the KV-cache and runs the entire attention computation (the QK and ScoreV matrix multiplications) in FP8 (e4m3 is the format used throughout this post)." On the calibration-free question the blog is explicit that scale=1.0 is the evaluated configuration: "Important: All evaluations use per-tensor uncalibrated quantization scales (i.e., scale = 1.0). This is the simplest possible configuration — no calibration data, no per-head tuning — and represents the worst-case scenario for accuracy." Headline result: "FP8 KV-cache and attention quantization introduces at most 1-2 points of accuracy degradation, with the lowest recovery at 97% (GPQA:Diamond, BF16 model)." Stated exceptions: "The main exceptions are workloads where prefill dominates on head_dim = 256 , hybrid models whose small sliding-window layers should be left in BF16, and models or backends that show persistent uncalibrated accuracy loss, where calibration remains important."

title: Per-token-head dynamic (calibration-free) INT8 / FP8 / INT4 KV scales shipped in vLLM 0.29.0
detail: vLLM's `KVQuantMode` IntEnum enumerates the shipped modes with their scale granularity, verbatim: `INT8_PER_TOKEN_HEAD = 2  # per-token-head dynamic scales for int8`, `FP8_PER_TOKEN_HEAD = 3  # per-token-head dynamic scales for fp8`, `INT4_PER_TOKEN_HEAD = 4  # packed 2×int4/byte, RHT + asymmetric zp`, `NVFP4 = 5  # packed fp4 data + fp8 block scales`, and the four TurboQuant modes `TURBOQUANT_K8V4 = 6`, `TURBOQUANT_4BIT_NC = 7`, `TURBOQUANT_K3V4_NC = 8`, `TURBOQUANT_3BIT_NC = 9` documented as "Hadamard-rotated Lloyd-Max quant, packed K+V per slot." The runtime (not checkpoint) scale computation is logged from `vllm/config/cache.py`: "Dynamic per-token-head scales will be computed at runtime." The same file's non-per-token-head branch states the older caveat verbatim: "Meanwhile, it may cause accuracy drop without a proper scaling factor". This closes the per-token/per-channel-scale question for vLLM: KIVI-style asymmetry is now expressible without calibration.

title: INT4 per-token-head KV cache quantisation merged into vLLM
detail: Merged by tdoublep on Jun 24, 2026 ("tdoublep merged 72 commits into vllm-project:main"), merge commit `70749fd`. The PR body verbatim: "Based on PR: #40633 / Changed to only INT4_PER_TOKEN_HEAD". It carried GSM8K evidence in-body as an HTML table whose individual cell values were retrieved (cell sequence: `gsm8k` / `3` / `flexible-extract` / `5` / `exact_match` / `↑` / `0.912` / `±` / `0.0273`; reproduced here space-joined rather than as one contiguous source string). The shipped kernel is documented in the source header (read locally at /tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/int4_per_token_head.py): "INT4 packs two 4-bit values per cache byte, pre-rotates with a single RHT, and hides a 4-bit zero-point in the scale's low mantissa bits — too different from the core kernel to share it." Accuracy is guarded by a shipped test that compares logprobs against a bf16 baseline for all three per-token-head dtypes (tests/models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py).

title: TurboQuant sub-4-bit online KV backend merged in vLLM (Hadamard rotation + Lloyd-Max)
detail: Merged ("vllm-bot merged 10 commits into vllm-project:main"). Body verbatim: "TurboQuant adds online KV cache compression to vLLM's v1 attention backend using PolarQuant (WHT rotation + Lloyd-Max scalar quantization) for keys and uniform quantization for values. All quantization happens at store time via fused Triton kernels — no offline calibration, model changes, or weight modifications required. Just set --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k8v4 ." The PR body reports results on the exact target model, verbatim: "Compression Presets (Qwen3-4B, head_dim=128)" with "Baseline: GSM8K 0.900, NIAH 100%. Measured on Qwen/Qwen3-4B with 5-shot GSM8K (200q) and NIAH (512-32K, 77 probes)." Per-preset GSM8K: k8v4 = 0.860 (2.6x), 4bit_nc = 0.840 (3.8x), k3v4_nc = 0.780 (4.3x), 3bit_nc = 0.720 (4.9x). (See HW-1: the accompanying performance table is 4-GPU.)

title: `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` shipped — per-layer precision escape hatch
detail: Merged; the flag is also documented in the vLLM FP8 KV-cache blog, verbatim: "We added --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers ( vllm#33695 ) to allow for hybrid settings." The blog states the rationale verbatim: "Models like GPT-OSS use some layers with sliding window attention, where tokens attend to a fixed window size, for example 128 tokens. Here FP8 overheads cannot be amortized. Therefore, keeping those layers in BF16 is actually faster than quantizing them... Furthermore, if some layers are particularly sensitive to quantization, this feature allows skipping those layers." It is present in vLLM 0.29.0 source (`vllm/config/cache.py: kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)`) and documented at https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.28.0/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache/ as accepting "either layer indices or layer-type names".

title: fp8_e5m2 KV cache unblocked for weight-only-quantised checkpoints
detail: Merged by yewentao256 Jun 18, 2026. Body verbatim: "_init_kv_cache_quant rejects --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2 for every quantized checkpoint with \"fp8_e5m2 kv-cache is not supported with fp8 checkpoints\". But weight-only checkpoints (INT4/INT8 compressed-tensors, AWQ, GPTQ) carry no fp8 KV scales and are not fp8. On Ampere, where fp8_e5m2 is the only fp8 KV cache dtype that runs at all ( fp8_e4m3 is unsupported by the hardware), this makes fp8 KV cache unreachable for every weight-quantized model." This is the clearest shipped statement of the e4m3-vs-e5m2 hardware split: e5m2 is the Ampere-compatible format, e4m3 is not.

title: KIVI — per-channel K, per-token V, tuning-free 2-bit KV cache
detail: The canonical answer to the per-channel/per-token scale question. Abstract verbatim: "Our findings indicate that the key cache should be quantized per-channel, i.e., group elements along the channel dimension and quantize them together. In contrast, the value cache should be quantized per-token. From this analysis, we developed a tuning-free 2bit KV cache quantization algorithm named KIVI." Also: "KIVI can enable Llama, Falcon, and Mistral models to maintain almost the same quality while using 2.6× less peak memory (including model weight)." Submission history shows v1 5 Feb 2024, v2 25 Jul 2024 (no 2025-2026 revision).

title: KVQuant — per-channel key quant, pre-RoPE key quant, non-uniform datatypes, per-vector dense-and-sparse outliers
detail: The canonical reference for outlier handling in KV quantisation and the source of the "dense-and-sparse" idea. Abstract verbatim: "(i) Per-Channel Key Quantization, where we adjust the dimension along which we quantize the Key activations to better match the distribution; (ii) Pre-RoPE Key Quantization, where we quantize Key activations before the rotary positional embedding to mitigate its impact on quantization; (iii) Non-Uniform KV Cache Quantization, where we derive per-layer sensitivity-weighted non-uniform datatypes that better represent the distributions; and (iv) Per-Vector Dense-and-Sparse Quantization, where we isolate outliers separately for each vector to minimize skews in quantization ranges." Result verbatim: "we achieve < 0.1 perplexity degradation with 3-bit quantization on both Wikitext-2 and C4". Submission history runs to v6 on 28 May 2025.

title: TurboQuant — data-oblivious rotation + per-coordinate Lloyd-Max quantiser, near-optimal distortion
detail: The theoretical paper underlying vLLM's shipped turboquant_* dtypes. Abstract verbatim: "TurboQuant achieves this by randomly rotating input vectors, inducing a concentrated Beta distribution on coordinates, and leveraging the near-independence property of distinct coordinates in high dimensions to simply apply optimal scalar quantizers per each coordinate." And: "Experimental results validate our theoretical findings, showing that for KV cache quantization, we achieve absolute quality neutrality with 3.5 bits per channel and marginal quality degradation with 2.5 bits per channel." The full HTML explains that the non-integer bit rates come from outlier splitting, verbatim: "These non-integer bit precisions result from our strategy of splitting channels into outlier and non-outlier sets, and applying two independent instances of TurboQuant to each, allocating higher bit precision to outliers." and "in our 2.5-bit setup, 32 outlier channels are quantized at 3 bits, while the remaining 96 channels use 2 bits, leading to an effective bit precision of ( 32 × 3 + 96 × 2 ) / 128 = 2.5". Note the paper's own setup is modest: "All experiments are performed using a single NVIDIA A100 GPU."

title: KVarN — calibration-free variance-normalised KV quantiser that targets autoregressive error accumulation
detail: The most recent (Jun 2026) published answer to the "quantized-KV attention error" sub-question. Abstract verbatim: "KV-cache quantization can help improve this, but current methods are evaluated under prefill-like settings and errors behave differently under autoregressive decoding. We show that in the latter regime, quantization errors accumulate across timesteps, driven primarily by incorrect token scales. We introduce KVarN, a calibration-free KV-cache quantizer that applies a Hadamard rotation followed by a dual-scaling variance normalization across both axes of the K and V matrices." Claim verbatim: "KVarN establishes a new state-of-theart for KV-cache quantization on generative benchmarks, including MATH500, AIME24 and HumanEval, at 2-bit precision." A vLLM implementation is claimed available in the abstract.

title: QAQ — keys and values have distinct quantisation sensitivity; dedicated outlier handling
detail: Abstract verbatim: "We theoretically demonstrate that key cache and value cache exhibit distinct sensitivities to quantization, leading to the formulation of separate quantization strategies for their non-uniform quantization. Through the integration of dedicated outlier handling, as well as an improved attention-aware approach, QAQ achieves up to 10x the compression ratio of the KV cache size with a neglectable impact on model performance." QAQ is notable for being absent from both engine trees (see OPEN-12).

title: FP8 long-context accuracy collapse traced to Tensor-Core accumulation precision, and fixed (two-level accumulation)
detail: This is the strongest published entry on "quantized-KV attention error" as a *kernel numerics* problem rather than a storage-format problem. Verbatim: "Hopper's FP8 Tensor Cores are documented as accumulating into FP32 registers, but in practice the intermediate accumulation loses precision when the contraction dimension is large... When the contraction dimension reaches 100K or more, this imprecise accumulation causes drastic numerical errors. Concretely, in long context inference, during the Softmax(AttnScore) * V matmul, the contraction dimension corresponds to the context lengths. Empirically, we found that this can lead to accuracy regressions from 91% (BF16) to 13% (FP8) on a long-context needle-in-a-haystack task." The fix verbatim: "we added a two-level accumulation strategy (see SageAttention2 ) that writes the partially accumulated results into an actual FP32 register ( flash-attention#104 ), which brought the FP8 accuracy back to 89%." Residual cost verbatim: "On the downside, this two-level accumulation increases the register pressure and causes slowdowns during prefill... however, for head dimensions larger than 128, the prefill performance remains behind BF16."

title: Public doc for calibration-free FP8 KV dtype semantics and layer skipping
detail: The shipped user-facing contract. Verbatim: "No calibration (default scales): All quantization scales are set to 1.0." and "[Recommended] Calibration with a dataset (via llm-compressor)". The per-head limitation is stated verbatim: "Per-attention-head quantization is currently available only with the Flash Attention backend and requires the calibration pathway provided by llm-compressor ." Note the doc's option list still covers only 3 of the values `CacheDType` accepts — see OPEN-11. ---

title: vLLM native CPU KV offload (`OffloadingConnector`), shipped in vLLM 0.11.0
detail: The vLLM team describes the shipped asynchronous offloading connector with a bundled CPU backend. Verbatim: "The offloading connector is bundled with a CPU backend, enabling native CPU offloading of KV data in vLLM." and "In this post, we will describe the new KV cache offloading feature that was introduced in vLLM 0.11.0." Reported gains: "The results demonstrate that loading KV values from the CPU reduces TTFT by X2-X22 , depending on the prompt size." and "We observe that the throughput increases by up to X9".

title: `--kv-offloading-size` / `--kv-offloading-backend native` CLI
detail: Merged by NickLucche 2026-01-12. PR body verbatim: "This PR replaces the OffloadingConnector size configuration from num_cpu_blocks to cpu_bytes_to_use. This allows for a more intuitive space allocation (per vLLM instance, across workers)." The vLLM blog documents the flag it produced, verbatim: "--kv_offloading_backend native --kv_offloading_size <size_in_GB>". The local vLLM 0.29.0 tree confirms both flags are registered in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` (`"--kv-offloading-size"`, `"--kv-offloading-backend"`) with `kv_offloading_size: float | None = None` defaulting off.

title: vLLM multi-tier KV offloading framework (`TieringOffloadingSpec`)
detail: Merged by orozery 2026-05-13. Verbatim from the PR body: "Adds a hierarchical (tiered) KV cache offloading framework under vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ , extending the existing single-tier CPU offloading with support for chained secondary tiers (e.g., storage, network)." It adds `SecondaryTierManager`, `CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager`, `TieringOffloadingManager` and `TieringOffloadingSpec`.

title: Filesystem (NVMe) secondary tier + shipped usage guide
detail: The shipped vLLM 0.29.0 doc states verbatim: "Two specs are available, selected by the `spec_name` key in `kv_connector_extra_config`: - `CPUOffloadingSpec` (default): single CPU tier. Completed GPU blocks are copied into pinned host memory. - `TieringOffloadingSpec`: multi-tier. A CPU primary tier plus one or more secondary tiers." and "Only the CPU primary tier has direct GPU access. Secondary tiers cannot read from or write to GPU memory; all GPU↔secondary transfers are staged through the CPU primary tier." Tier types shipped: `fs`, `obj` (S3-compatible via NIXL OBJ), `p2p` (RDMA via NIXL).

title: Batched KV swap copies via `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`
detail: Merged by orozery 2026-04-03. Verbatim: "Replace per-layer per-block swap_blocks calls in the KV cache offloading handler with a single swap_blocks_batch call that submits all copies in one driver invocation. On CUDA 12.8+ this uses cuMemcpyBatchAsync ; on older CUDA/ROCm it falls back to a flat cudaMemcpyAsync loop with cudaMemcpyDefault . Zero extra GPU memory. No behavior change." Benchmark hardware stated in the PR: "Hardware: 8xH100 80GB HBM3, CUDA 12.8/12.9."

title: SGLang HiCache three-tier design and flags
detail: Verbatim: "Inspired by the classic three-level cache design of modern CPUs, HiCache organizes GPU memory as L1, host memory as L2, and distributed storage as L3." Shipped flags include `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, `--hicache-ratio`, `--hicache-size`, `--hicache-io-backend {direct,kernel}`, `--hicache-mem-layout {layer_first,page_first,page_first_direct}`, `--hicache-write-policy {write_back,write_through,write_through_selective}`, `--hicache-storage-backend {file,mooncake,hf3fs,nixl,aibrix,dynamic}`, `--enable-lmcache`. Documented constraint verbatim: "The value of this parameter must be greater than 1, as the current implementation requires the host memory allocated for the KV cache to be larger than the device memory allocated for the KV cache."

title: HiCache storage backend runtime attach/detach
detail: A dedicated shipped doc exists for attaching/detaching the L3 backend without restarting the server; referenced from the best-practices doc verbatim: "Besides configuring `--hicache-storage-backend` at startup, SGLang also supports **runtime attach/detach** of the HiCache storage backend (no restart required) via HTTP admin endpoints."

title: Mooncake KVCache-centric disaggregated architecture
detail: Verbatim abstract: "It also leverages the underutilized CPU, DRAM, and SSD resources of the GPU cluster to implement a disaggregated cache of KVCache." and "Compared to the baseline method, Mooncake can achieve up to a 525% increase in throughput in certain simulated scenarios while adhering to SLOs." v4 revised 2025-09-03 (inside the priority window).

title: LMCache as an out-of-GPU KV caching layer
detail: Verbatim: "We present LMCACHE, the first and so far the most efficient open-source KV caching solution, which extracts and stores KV caches generated by modern LLM engines (vLLM and SGLang) out of the GPU memory and shares them across engines and queries." Its design claims verbatim: "(1) highly optimized KV cache data movement powered by batched data movement operations, compute and I/O pipelining; (2) a modular KV cache connector component, decoupling LMCACHE from the rapid evolution of inference engines; (3) a first-class control API for flexible cache orchestration across GPU, CPU, storage, and network layers."

title: CacheGen KV cache compression + streaming
detail: Canonical reference for tiered KV transfer under bandwidth limits. Title verified by fetching the abstract page: "CacheGen: KV Cache Compression and Streaming for Fast Large Language Model Serving" (submitted 11 Oct 2023, v6 19 Jul 2024). Its hardware is a single A40 (see HW section note) — it is NOT ruled out by the target hardware.

title: Pensieve multi-tier GPU+CPU conversation-state caching
detail: Canonical multi-tier KV caching reference. Verbatim: "Pensieve's multi-tier caching strategy can utilize both GPU and CPU memory to efficiently store and retrieve cached data." Reported result verbatim: "Our evaluation shows that Pensieve can achieve 1.14 - 3.0× the throughput of vLLM and TensorRT-LLM and significantly reduce latency."

title: py-kvcache external NVMe KV offload connector for vLLM
detail: Published 2026-09-10, inside the priority window and run on a single GPU with Qwen3-4B. Verbatim: "These findings motivate py-kvcache, a vLLM KV Offload connector with asynchronous direct I/O, bounded shared staging, and scheduler-aware preloading, which starts disk reads while requests are still waiting, overlapping with compute. At 80k tokens, py-kvcache loading from disk is 2.0x faster than LMCache, with preloading contributing 1.34x." Setup verbatim: "Although the nodes have multiple GPUs, all our experiments use a single GPU." and "Experiments use Llama 3.2 3B Instruct and Qwen3 4B Instruct 2507".

title: vLLM `MooncakeStoreConnector` (distributed KV store offload)
detail: Shipped connector doc. Verbatim: "Unlike `MooncakeConnector` which does direct point-to-point KV transfer between prefiller and decoder, MooncakeStoreConnector enables KV cache offloading to an external distributed store, supporting: - **CPU/disk offloading**: Extend effective KV cache capacity by offloading to CPU memory or disk via Mooncake's transfer engine." and "**Single-node and multi-node deployment**: Works both as a standalone KV cache extension and in disaggregated prefill-decode setups."

title: vLLM `ECCPUConnector` (CPU tier for the multimodal encoder cache)
detail: Verbatim: "`ECCPUConnector` extends the GPU-based encoder cache with a CPU tier: it offloads encoder outputs (`encoder_cache[mm_hash]`) to a shared `/dev/shm` mmap region so later steps and later requests reuse them instead of recomputing." Local CPU-tier mode needs no extra packages; the doc states verbatim: "the gate-off code path (`cpu/connector.py`, `cpu/scheduler/`, `cpu/worker/`, `cpu/common.py`) imports no `nixl`/`zmq`/`msgspec`, enforced by a repo test".

title: vLLM `FlexKVConnectorV1` (CPU/SSD/remote multi-level KV)
detail: Registered in the shipped factory verbatim: `KVConnectorFactory.register_connector("FlexKVConnectorV1", "vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.flexkv_connector", "FlexKVConnectorV1")`. The connector source states verbatim: "FlexKV is a distributed KV Store and multi-level cache management system designed for ultra-large-scale LLM inference. It supports offloading KV cache to CPU memory, SSD, and remote storage."

title: `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` eager-registration + final-flush bug fixed
detail: Merged by ivanium 2026-09-02. Verbatim from the PR body: "Register completed CPU blocks through BlockPool so eager offload entries are discoverable by prefix-cache lookup. Preserve fine-grained hashes when copying GPU cache metadata to CPU blocks. Queue confirmed blocks that remain when a request finishes, batch them into the next connector metadata, and release their references safely on reset." This closes bug report #53498.

title: HiCache host tier must be larger than device tier (documented constraint)
detail: Verbatim: "L1 and L2 are private to a single inference instance; only L3 can be shared. Host memory cannot be pooled across instances or across hosts, not even for two instances on the same node. Raising `--hicache-ratio` or `--hicache-size` only enlarges the instance's own private L2." This is a shipped design answer to "can I pool host memory across instances?" — the answer is no.

title: Tiered lookup resolution — HIT_PENDING returned when a KV promotion is triggered
detail: Merged by orozery 2026-08-12; PR body states verbatim "fixes #51439". The RFC it closes describes the problem verbatim: "KV lookups in tiered offloading are considered a HIT only when the KV's materialize in the CPU tier. As an extreme case example, for some request that has none of its KV blocks are in the CPU, but has all of its KV secondary tiers, this 2 Phase lookup approach results in unnecessary tier -> CPU loads." RFC #51439 is recorded as Closed and linked to "#51840".

title: HERALD — CPU-GPU cooperative KV cache retrieval for block-diffusion LLMs
detail: Published 2026-06-19 (v2 2026-08-03). Verbatim abstract: "Offloading the cache to CPU DRAM restores capacity, but the limited PCIe bandwidth forces state-of-the-art offloading systems to pair it with sparse attention, fetching only a small critical subset of the cache to the GPU." Reported result verbatim (from the abstract as retrieved by delegated retrieval): "HERALD sustains near-lossless accuracy at a 5% KV budget and reaches up to 2.28x the decode throughput of GPU-only serving, with gains that widen with context length." Its own PCIe bottleneck measurement is quoted under ABANDONED-19.

title: KVDrive — holistic multi-tier (GPU / host DRAM / SSD) KV cache management
detail: Published 2026-05-18. Verbatim abstract: "We present KVDrive, a holistic multi-tier KV cache management system spanning GPU memory, host DRAM, and SSD. Unlike prior work that pursues greater sparsity through algorithmic refinements, KVDrive tackles the problem from a systems perspective - jointly orchestrating cache placement, pipeline scheduling, and cross-tier coordination to sustain high-throughput inference under tight GPU budgets." Reported result verbatim (delegated retrieval): "The system achieves up to 1.74x higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art works while preserving accuracy." Its explicit rebuttal of CPU-attention offloading is quoted under ABANDONED-20.

title: Tutti — GPU-centric KV cache object store for SSD-backed KV cache
detail: Published 2026-05-05. Verbatim abstract: "This paper presents Tutti, an efficient SSD-backed KV caching solution that eliminates CPU intervention from the critical data and I/O control paths between HBM and SSDs. At the core of Tutti is a GPU-centric KV cache object store, in which the CPU is only responsible for [...]". Reported result verbatim (delegated retrieval): "compared with the SOTA GDS-enabled SSD-backed solution, Tutti reduces TTFT by 78.3% under strict SLO constraints and improves the achievable request rate by 2x."

title: IMPRESS — importance-informed multi-tier prefix KV storage (single GPU + one SSD)
detail: Published at USENIX FAST 2025. I verified the title on the USENIX presentation page verbatim: "IMPRESS: An Importance-Informed Multi-Tier Prefix KV Storage System for Large Language Model Inference", and confirmed the PDF exists (HTTP 200, 1,418,658 bytes, "PDF document, version 1.7, 8 pages"). The evaluation hardware, verbatim as retrieved by delegated retrieval from §6.1 of the PDF: "Our experiments are performed on a server with 2[×] AMD EPYC 7763 CPUs (64 cores), 128 GB DRAM, one NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80GB HBM, and one 2TB Intel SSD whose measured read throughput is around 5GB/s. The GPU and CPU are connected via PCIe 4.0[×]16." (The `[×]` glyphs are math-font multiplication signs that the extractor could not render; they are marked rather than silently smoothed.) This is the closest published match to the target researcher's shape: one GPU plus one local SSD.

title: `CachePolicyFactory` — pluggable/out-of-tree eviction policies for the CPU offload tier
detail: Merged by orozery 2026-07-29. Verbatim from the PR body: "CPUOffloadingManager resolves eviction_policy ("lru"/"arc") through a private, closed dict in manager.py with no way for an out-of-tree package to plug in its own CachePolicy implementation by name, the same way OffloadingSpecFactory and KVConnectorFactory already let external specs/connectors register themselves." The shipped vLLM 0.29.0 doc confirms the result verbatim: "`eviction_policy` resolves through `CachePolicyFactory` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/factory.py`), which pre-registers the built-in `lru` and `arc` policies."

title: MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeek-V2)
detail: The canonical architectural KV reduction. Retrieved title "DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model"; abstract states verbatim: "MLA guarantees efficient inference through significantly compressing the Key-Value (KV) cache into a latent vector, while DeepSeekMoE enables training strong models at an economical cost through sparse computation. Compared with DeepSeek 67B, DeepSeek-V2 achieves significantly stronger performance, and meanwhile saves 42.5% of training costs, reduces the KV cache by 93.3%, and boosts the maximum generation throughput to 5.76 times."

title: MQA (Multi-Query Attention)
detail: The original KV-head-reduction design and the baseline every later scheme compares against. Verbatim: "We propose a variant called multi-query attention, where the keys and values are shared across all of the different attention \"heads\", greatly reducing the size of these tensors and hence the memory bandwidth requirements of incremental decoding. We verify experimentally that the resulting models can indeed be much faster to decode, and incur only minor quality degradation from the baseline."

title: GQA (Grouped-Query Attention)
detail: Closes the "how do I get MQA's memory win on an existing checkpoint" question. Verbatim: "we (1) propose a recipe for uptraining existing multi-head language model checkpoints into models with MQA using 5% of original pre-training compute, and (2) introduce grouped-query attention (GQA), a generalization of multi-query attention which uses an intermediate (more than one, less than number of query heads) number of key-value heads. We show that uptrained GQA achieves quality close to multi-head attention with comparable speed to MQA."

title: DMC (Dynamic Memory Compression)
detail: The reference "learned, per-head/per-layer online KV compression ratio" result. Verbatim: "we propose Dynamic Memory Compression (DMC), a method for online key-value cache compression at inference time. Most importantly, the model learns to apply different compression ratios in different heads and layers." and "DMC preserves the original downstream performance with up to 4x cache compression, outperforming up-trained grouped-query attention (GQA) and key-value eviction policies (H$_2$O, TOVA). GQA and DMC can be even combined to obtain compounded gains." Note: published, but NOT shipped in any of the three engines surveyed (see ABANDONED-1/2).

title: MiniCache
detail: Depth-dimension KV merging, the technique that most "KV merging" papers build on. Verbatim: "we present a simple yet effective approach, called MiniCache, to compress the KV cache across layers from a novel depth perspective, significantly reducing the memory footprint for LLM inference. Our approach is based on the observation that KV cache states exhibit high similarity between the adjacent layers in the middle-to-deep portion of LLMs. To facilitate merging, we propose disentangling the states into the magnitude and direction components, interpolating the directions of the state vectors while preserving their lengths unchanged."

title: YOCO (You Only Cache Once)
detail: Verbatim: "We introduce a decoder-decoder architecture, YOCO, for large language models, which only caches key-value pairs once. It consists of two components, i.e., a cross-decoder stacked upon a self-decoder. The self-decoder efficiently encodes global key-value (KV) caches that are reused by the cross-decoder via cross-attention." and "The design substantially reduces GPU memory demands, yet retains global attention capability."

title: CLA (Cross-Layer Attention)
detail: Verbatim: "we show that it is possible to take Multi-Query Attention a step further by also sharing key and value heads between adjacent layers, yielding a new attention design we call Cross-Layer Attention (CLA). With CLA, we find that it is possible to reduce the size of the KV cache by another 2x while maintaining nearly the same accuracy as unmodified MQA. In experiments training 1B- and 3B-parameter models from scratch, we demonstrate that CLA provides a Pareto improvement over the memory/accuracy tradeoffs which are possible with traditional MQA".

title: Palu (low-rank KV cache with fused kernels)
detail: The canonical hidden-dimension (low-rank) KV compression result. Verbatim: "This paper presents a hidden dimension compression approach called Palu, a KV-Cache compression framework that utilizes low-rank projection to reduce inference-time LLM memory usage. Palu decomposes the linear layers into low-rank matrices, caches compressed intermediate states, and reconstructs the full keys and values on the fly." and "Palu compresses KV-Cache by 50% while maintaining strong accuracy and delivering up to 1.89x on the RoPE-based attention module."

title: xKV (cross-layer aligned singular vector extraction)
detail: Verbatim: "We show, via Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), that the dominant singular vectors of KV-Cache are well aligned across layers. Motivated by this observation, we propose xKV, a post-training compression method that jointly factorizes grouped-layer KV-Cache into a shared low-rank subspace, substantially reducing KV-Cache memory. Across widely used LLMs, xKV achieves up to 8x KV-Cache compression while preserving accuracy on long-context tasks and in multi-turn settings."

title: X-EcoMLA (KV distillation / MLA upcycling)
detail: The "KV distillation" branch — converting a pretrained non-MLA model into MLA by post-training distillation instead of pre-training. Verbatim: "we propose X-EcoMLA to deploy post training distillation to enable the upcycling of Transformer-based attention into an efficient hybrid MLA variant through lightweight post-training adaptation, bypassing the need for extensive pre-training." and "for Llama3.2-1B-Instruct baseline, a 6.4x compression achieves the same average score by using only 3.6B training tokens and 70 GPU hours on AMD" (abstract retrieved text ends mid-sentence at the hardware name; quoted exactly as retrieved).

title: MTLA (Multi-head Temporal Latent Attention)
detail: KV merging inside a latent design (temporal axis). Verbatim: "This paper proposes Multi-head Temporal Latent Attention (MTLA), which further reduces the KV cache size along the temporal dimension, greatly lowering the memory footprint of self-attention inference. MTLA employs a hyper-network to dynamically merge temporally adjacent KV cache vectors."

title: vLLM ships a full MLA backend family
detail: Retrieved from the local vLLM source tree at `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main/docs/design/attention_backends.md` (this checkout contains 2026-era models incl. deepseek_v4, kimi_k3, gemma4), and the cited GitHub blob URL was **independently re-fetched and confirmed** (HTTP 200, page title "vllm/docs/design/attention_backends.md at main · vllm-project/vllm · GitHub", and the quoted heading "MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) Backends" is present in the retrieved blob HTML). Verbatim: "## MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) Backends" / "MLA uses separate backends for prefill and decode phases." / "MLA decode backends are selected using the standard `-ac.backend=<BACKEND>` argument (e.g., `FLASHMLA`, `TRITON_MLA`)." and for DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA: "default on NVIDIA is `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` on SM12x and `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` on other supported CUDA architectures."

title: vLLM ships YOCO-style cross-layer KV sharing (Gemma3n / Gemma4) behind a real flag
detail: Retrieved from the local vLLM tree, and the cited GitHub blob URL was **independently re-fetched and confirmed** (HTTP 200, page title "vllm/vllm/config/cache.py at main · vllm-project/vllm · GitHub", with the string `kv_sharing_fast_prefill` present in the retrieved blob HTML). The flag `kv_sharing_fast_prefill` is documented verbatim as: "In some KV sharing setups, e.g. YOCO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05254), some layers can skip tokens corresponding to prefill. This flag enables attention metadata for eligible layers to be overridden with metadata necessary for implementing this optimization in some models (e.g. Gemma3n)". The model-side split is implemented verbatim in `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py`: "# --- You Only Cache Once (YOCO) split for fast prefill ---" / "# Layers 0..(K-1) are self-decoder layers in YOCO" / "# Layers K..(N-1) are cross-decoder layers in YOCO", and in `gemma3n.py`: "# Layer idx 0-19 are self-decoder layers in You Only Cache Once (YOCO)" / "# Layer idx 20-30 are cross-decoder layers in YOCO". E2E test exists at `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill.py`.

title: CommonKV (training-free cross-layer KV compression by adjacent-parameter SVD sharing)
detail: Verbatim: "we propose CommonKV, a training-free method for cross-layer KV cache compression through adjacent parameters sharing. Inspired by the high similarity observed in cross-layer hidden states, we utilize Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to achieve weight sharing across adjacent parameters, resulting in a more easily mergeable latent KV cache." and "By integrating these approaches, we can ultimately achieve a 98\% compression ratio without significant performance loss."

title: TurboQuant merged into vLLM (learned/optimized KV vector quantizer)
detail: Retrieved PR page. Verbatim title: "[Attention Backend] TurboQuant: 2-bit KV cache compression with 4x capacity by vibhavagarwal5 · Pull Request #38479 · vllm-project/vllm · GitHub". The retrieved page payload contains the token `"state":"MERGED"` (matched on the retrieved HTML). This is the closest thing to a shipped "learned codebook / vector-quantized KV" in vLLM, and other open issues cite it as merged (see OPEN-8).

title: CLLA (lossless KV cache to 2%)
detail: Verbatim: "This work introduces a novel architecture, Cross-Layer Latent Attention (CLLA), aimed at compressing the KV cache to less than 2% of its original size while maintaining comparable performance levels. CLLA integrates multiple aspects of KV cache compression, including attention head/dimension reduction, layer sharing, and quantization techniques, into a cohesive framework." ---

title: vLLM v1 KV connector API and the 9-connector suite
detail: The v1 connector API is shipped and the docs enumerate the supported set. Verbatim: "Now supports 9 types of connectors:" followed by ExampleConnector, LMCacheConnectorV1, NixlConnector, MooncakeConnector, MoRIIOConnector, MultiConnector, OffloadingConnector, FlexKVConnectorV1 (and LMCacheMPConnector described in the LMCacheConnectorV1 bullet). The same page states for NixlConnector: "refer to `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` for the example usage of NixlConnector disaggregated prefilling which support fully async send/recv." The registry in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/factory.py` (inspected in the extracted tree at `/tmp/kvsrc/vllm-main`) registers 18 names: ExampleConnector, ExampleHiddenStatesConnector, LMCacheConnectorV1, LMCacheMPConnector, NixlConnector, NixlPullConnector, NixlPushConnector, MultiConnector, MoRIIOConnector, OffloadingConnector, DecodeBenchConnector, MooncakeConnector, MooncakeStoreConnector, FlexKVConnectorV1, SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, HF3FSKVConnector.

title: NixlPushConnector — push-mode cross-instance KV transfer
detail: Verbatim: "The default NIXL connector is **pull-based**: the decode (D) instance reads KV blocks from the prefill (P) instance via `NIXL READ` after prefill completes. `NixlPushConnector` adds a **push-based** alternative in which P writes the KV blocks directly into D's pre-allocated memory via `NIXL WRITE`." The doc also specifies the dedicated per-TP-rank background thread: "``NixlPushConnectorWorker`` introduces a single dedicated background thread per worker (i.e. per TP rank), named ``nixl-push-writer``." This is a shipped connector name (`"NixlPushConnector"` in the factory registry).

title: Mooncake Store Connector heterogeneous-TP KV sharing
detail: The tracked problem and the merged fix are stated by the RFC author, z-zanez, in vLLM issue #55598 (retrieved): "Mooncake Store originally tied object keys and payload layout to the local TP rank. Two vLLM instances using the same model but different TP sizes therefore produced different shard counts, KV-head ranges, and namespaces and could not reuse each other's persisted KV cache." The fix: "[KV Connector] Support heterogeneous TP sharing in Mooncake Store Connector #53129 adds a common Store TP layout for Full Attention. Local TP ranks map to stable Store shards, allowing supported TP4/TP2/TP1 instances and multiple Prefill TP sizes to reuse and update the same Store entries." All three PR pages display the merged badge. PR #53129 title as retrieved: "[KV Connector] Support heterogeneous TP sharing in Mooncake Store Connector by z-zanez".

title: vLLM OffloadingConnector P2P tier — instance-to-instance KV exchange
detail: Verbatim: "The P2P tier (`type: "p2p"`) shares completed KV blocks between vLLM instances over RDMA via NIXL. Each instance binds a control socket on `host:port` and exchanges blocks directly with peers — no shared filesystem required." The merging PR is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47636 "[KVOffload][P2P] Well-known default host/port env vars and per-DP-rank control port by liranschour", whose retrieved page payload contains `"state":"MERGED"`. The same guide documents the P2P tier fields `backends` (default `["UCX"]`) and `num_threads`.

title: Cross-process KV cache key determinism (dedup across instances)
detail: Verbatim: "KV cache sharing between multiple vLLM instances using the same `root_dir` (e.g., via a shared PVC) works by default: `NONE_HASH` (the chain-hash seed for block content hashes) is derived from a fixed default seed, so identical token content produces identical block filenames across instances. To use a custom shared seed instead, set the `PYTHONHASHSEED` environment variable to the same value on every instance." The documented exception is also stated verbatim: "The exception is the non-cryptographic `xxhash` and `xxhash_cbor` values of `--prefix-caching-hash-algo`, which seed `NONE_HASH` randomly per process so the seed stays unpredictable."

title: NIXL KV cache lease renewal
detail: Verbatim: "The lease renewal mechanism addresses both problems simultaneously. P grants a **short initial lease** (default 30s) when prefill completes. While a request is **queued or in-flight** on D, D **periodically sends heartbeats** to P extending the lease." The doc attributes the mechanism: "This mechanism was introduced in [PR #41383](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41383)." (PR #41383 itself was not fetched — cited only as quoted text inside this retrieved doc.) Also verbatim on the transport-agnostic heartbeat: "The notification medium is backend-specific, with automatic fallback from IB/RoCE to TCP already handled by NIXL."

title: SGLang HiCache — hierarchical KV with cross-instance L3 sharing
detail: Verbatim: "Inspired by the classic three-level cache design of modern CPUs, HiCache organizes GPU memory as L1, host memory as L2, and distributed storage as L3." and "When data is written back from L2 to L3, only data not already present in L3 is transferred. KV caches stored in L3 can then be shared across all SGLang instances in the cluster (depending on the L3 backend implementation)". The available L3 backends are stated verbatim: "Distributed backends such as mooncake , hf3fs , nixl and aibrix give cluster-wide scope, but only when every instance is pointed at the same namespace and configuration."

The PR touches `docs/fern/pages/cli/kv-aware-routing/overview.mdx`, i.e. the KV-aware routing documentation is part of the shipped change (reviewer comment retrieved: "In `@docs/fern/pages/cli/kv-aware-routing/overview.mdx`:").
